definition_zh: 诙谐的；幽默的；滑稽的；爱开玩笑的
definition_en: funny or amusing, or describing a person who likes to make people laugh
core_image: 把一件平常的事讲得让人笑出声
scene: 课堂上气氛很沉闷。The teacher told a humorous story and the whole class laughed.
sceneCN: 这里 humorous 是「诙谐的、引人发笑的」（第 1 个义项：内容有趣好笑）；句意：老师讲了一个幽默的故事，全班都笑了。

derivatives.zh: 幽默；由词根 humor 加后缀而来，指可笑的气质或内容
诙谐地；幽默地；形容词加副词后缀
幽默作家；词根加表人的后缀

senses.title: Funny and amusing
senses.definition: funny and making people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 有趣的、让人发笑的
senses.example: He kept a humorous tone even in serious talks.
senses.exampleCN: 即使在严肃谈话中他也保持幽默的语气。
senses.why: Humor is the substance that makes people laugh, so the adjective simply says the thing is full of that substance.
senses.whyCN: humor 本身指可笑的东西，形容词只是说这件事充满了这种东西，所以能引人发笑。

senses.title: Playful in manner
senses.definition: describing a person who often jokes and sees the funny side
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人爱开玩笑、总看到滑稽的一面
senses.example: My uncle is a humorous man at family dinners.
senses.exampleCN: 家宴上我叔叔是个爱开玩笑的人。
senses.why: The word moves from content to person: someone whose speech is constantly full of humor.
senses.whyCN: 词义从内容移到人：某人说话总是充满幽默感。

senses.title: Comically odd or exaggerated
senses.definition: odd or exaggerated in an amusing way
senses.definitionCN: 以好笑的方式显得古怪或夸张
senses.example: The film gives a humorous picture of office life.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影对办公室生活做了滑稽的刻画。
senses.why: When a portrayal exaggerates reality until it becomes funny, the result is labeled humorous.
senses.whyCN: 当描写把现实夸张到令人发笑时，成果就被贴上幽默的标签。

senses.title: Intended as a joke
senses.definition: said or done in a joking way rather than seriously
senses.definitionCN: 以玩笑方式说出或做出，而非当真
senses.example: It was a humorous comment, not a real criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是句玩笑话，不是真的批评。
senses.why: An utterance can carry humor as its purpose rather than its effect, so the adjective marks intent.
senses.whyCN: 话语可以以幽默为目的而不只是效果，形容词由此标记意图。

intro.en: Humorous comes from Latin humor, bodily fluid, through Old French and English humor. The four bodily fluids of medieval medicine were thought to shape mood, and a moody or capricious temperament came to be called humor, from which the modern sense of comedy developed.
intro.cn: humorous 源自拉丁语 humor「体液」，经古法语与英语 humor 传入。中世纪医学认为四种体液决定性情，「反复无常的脾气」被称为 humor，现代「滑稽可笑」的义项由此发展而来。

items.en: Latin humor meant moisture or bodily fluid, one of the fluids ancient doctors believed controlled health and temper.
items.cn: 拉丁语 humor 指湿气或体液，古代医生认为这些液体控制健康与性情。

items.en: Old French humur carried the same bodily meaning into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 humur 带着同样的体液义传入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English humor first meant bodily fluid, then a fixed temper or mood, as in being in a good humor.
items.cn: 中古英语 humor 先指体液，后指固定的心境，如 in a good humor「心情好」。

items.en: By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries humor meant an odd or amusing temperament, then anything that provokes laughter.
items.cn: 十七八世纪起 humor 指古怪有趣的性情，进而指一切引人发笑之物。

items.en: Humorous was formed in the seventeenth century as the adjective of humor and spread through literature and everyday speech.
items.cn: humorous 于十七世纪作为 humor 的形容词被造出，经文学与日常用语传播开来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the humor family and a falsely similar word. The meaning group collects other words for things that make people laugh.
note.cn: 形近组收录 humor 词族与一个貌似相关的词；词义组收集其他表示引人发笑之物的词。

entries.definition: the quality of being amusing, or a person's mood.
entries.definitionCN: 幽默；心情。是本词的名词基础。

entries.definition: a writer or performer who specializes in humor.
entries.definitionCN: 幽默作家或演员。由词根加表人后缀构成。

entries.definition: the bone of the upper arm. It only looks and sounds similar; it is a Latin anatomy word, not related to jokes.
entries.definitionCN: 上臂骨。只是拼写与读音相近，属解剖学词汇，与玩笑无关。

entries.definition: amusing in a direct, everyday way; broader and more casual than humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 好笑的。比 humorous 更口语、更宽泛。

entries.definition: entertaining and making you smile, often more gently funny.
entries.definitionCN: 逗乐的。常指温和的、让人微笑的有趣。

entries.definition: clever and quick with words; funny through intelligence.
entries.definitionCN: 机智的。靠言语巧妙取胜的幽默。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build humorous from humor plus the adjective ending, and link the family of humor, humorist and humorousness.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 humorous 拆成 humor 加形容词后缀，并串起 humor、humorist 等词族。

normal.en: Split it: humor + -ous. Full of humor, so funny.
normal.cn: 拆开看：humor 加 -ous。充满幽默，所以好笑。

normal.en: Humorist is a humor artist; humorous is what the artist's work is.
normal.cn: humorist 是幽默艺术家；humorous 形容这位艺术家的作品。

normal.en: Latin humor was a body fluid; old doctors said your fluids set your mood, and a bright mood laughs easily.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 humor 是体液；旧时医生说体液决定心情，心情明快就容易发笑。

normal.en: in a good humor means in a good mood; the family never lost that old sense.
normal.cn: in a good humor 意为心情好；这个词族至今保留着那个旧义。

normal.en: Watch the trap: humerus is an arm bone, not a joke bone.
normal.cn: 小心陷阱：humerus 是臂骨，不是「笑骨」。

abstract.en: One image: a teacher lifts a dull lesson and the class bursts out laughing.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：老师把沉闷的课讲活了，全班笑出声。

abstract.en: Think of humor as a fluid that pours into a story and makes it lighter.
abstract.cn: 把 humor 想成一种液体，倒进故事里让它变轻快。

abstract.en: Feel the scale: witty is sharp, amusing is gentle, humorous is the neutral middle.
abstract.cn: 感受尺度：witty 尖锐、amusing 温和，humorous 居中。

examples.en: She wrote a humorous column about city life.
examples.cn: 她写了一个关于城市生活的幽默专栏。

examples.en: His humorous answer eased the tension in the room.
examples.cn: 他诙谐的回答缓和了屋里的紧张气氛。

examples.en: Good speeches often open with a humorous remark.
examples.cn: 好的演讲常以一句幽默的话开场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「有墨若斯」：肚里很有墨水的人若开口，就幽默了。

root: 拉丁语 humor「体液、湿气」，经古法语 humur 与中古英语 humor「体液→心境→滑稽可笑」，加形容词后缀 -ous 构成 humorous「幽默的」。词义演变路径为「体液→性情→引人发笑」。

sensesIntro.en: Humorous spreads from content to people to intent: a thing can be funny, a person can be fond of jokes, a portrayal can be comically exaggerated, and a remark can be meant as a joke rather than seriously.
sensesIntro.cn: humorous 从内容铺到人再到意图：事物可以有趣，人可以爱开玩笑，刻画可以滑稽夸张，话也可以只是玩笑而非当真。

core.en: A bright mood-fluid poured into a thing, a person or a remark, making it laughable.
core.cn: 把明快的性情之液倒进事物、人或话语，使其引人发笑。

branches.en: FUNNY CONTENT: a thing or remark that provokes laughter, on purpose or by effect.
branches.cn: 有趣的内容：故意或事实上引人发笑的事物或话语。

branches.en: PLAYFUL PERSON: someone who sees the funny side and jokes often.
branches.cn: 爱开玩笑的人：总看到滑稽一面、常开玩笑的人。

branches.en: COMIC PORTRAYAL: an exaggerated, amusing picture of reality.
branches.cn: 滑稽刻画：对现实夸张而有趣的描绘。

branches.en: TEMPER: the old sense of humor as mood survives in a humorous turn of mind.
branches.cn: 性情：humor 的旧义「心境」保存在幽默的气质里。

branches.en: TONE: humor as a stylistic register, light instead of heavy.
branches.cn: 风格：幽默作为一种笔调，轻盈而非沉重。

intro.en: Humorous is humor plus -ous. The family keeps the mood sense alive in phrases like in a good humor.
intro.cn: humorous 由 humor 加 -ous 构成。这个词族在 in a good humor 等短语里保留着心境的旧义。

latinIntro.en: Latin entries show the bodily-fluid noun that slowly turned into the comedy noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目展示那个由体液慢慢变成「滑稽」的名词。

items.example: The narrator keeps a humorous voice.
items.exampleCN: 叙述者保持着幽默的口吻。

items.example: She has a fine sense of humor.

items.meaning: a person who writes or performs humor
items.example: The humorist signed copies of his new book.
items.exampleCN: 那位幽默作家为读者签名。

items.example: He humorously called the office a zoo.
items.exampleCN: 他诙谐地把办公室比作动物园。

items.example: The essay's humorousness hides its serious point.
items.exampleCN: 文章的幽默感掩盖着严肃的论点。

items.example: Our good-humored guide joked all day.
items.exampleCN: 我们和气的导游一路说笑。

items.example: He spoke out of ill-humor.
items.exampleCN: 他是带着坏心情说话的。

items.meaning: relating to bodily fluids, in old medicine
items.example: Ancient doctors held a humoral theory of disease.
items.exampleCN: 古代医生信奉体液致病说。

definition_en: the number 100, or a very large number of things
core_image: 数到尽头的一整排一百个格子
scene: 操场上队伍很长。There were three hundred students at the sports meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 hundred 是「百」（第 1 个义项：数词一百）；句意：运动会上有三百名学生。

derivatives.zh: 第一百；由基数加序数后缀构成

senses.title: The number 100
senses.definition: the cardinal number 100
senses.definitionCN: 基数词一百
senses.example: The hall holds six hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 礼堂能容纳六百人。
senses.why: The word names the base counting unit; with a numeral before it, it does not take a plural s.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名基本计数单位，前面有数字时不加复数 s。

senses.title: Hundreds of: a large indefinite number
senses.definition: a very large but uncounted number of things
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大但未清点的事物
senses.example: Hundreds of birds flew over the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 数百只鸟飞过湖面。
senses.why: Take the round number and stretch it beyond exact counting: it becomes a vague marker of many.
senses.whyCN: 把整数延伸到清点之外，就变成表示「多」的模糊标记。

senses.title: A division of counting or age
senses.definition: a section of a number scale, or a century of age
senses.definitionCN: 数位上的百位，或以百年计的时段
senses.example: She is in her hundredth year.
senses.exampleCN: 她已年过九十九。
senses.why: The unit also slices scales: place value, years, or ordered positions like the hundredth.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位也用来切分刻度：数位、年份或第一百这样的序位。

senses.title: A perfect score or total
senses.definition: a complete score out of a hundred, or total agreement
senses.definitionCN: 百分制中的满分，或完全一致
senses.example: He gave the plan a hundred percent support.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这个计划百分之百支持。
senses.why: Because a hundred is the whole of a standard scale, it stands for completeness.
senses.whyCN: 一百是标准刻度的全部，所以可以代表完整、全部。

intro.en: Hundred comes from Old English hund, hundred, combined with -red, a count or reckoning. Germanic peoples counted by long hundreds of one hundred and twenty, and the word also named an old administrative district.
intro.cn: hundred 来自古英语 hund「百」加 -red「计数」。日耳曼人的「长百」为一百二十，该词也曾指古代的行政区。

items.en: The reconstructed form combines hund, ten, with a root redh, to count, giving the sense a count of ten decades.
items.cn: 重构形式由 hund「十」加 redh「计数」词根构成，意为「十个十的计数」。

items.en: Old English hundred meant both the number and a district of one hundred households used for taxes and courts.
items.cn: 古英语 hundred 既指数词，也指用于征税与司法的百户行政区。

items.en: Old Norse hundrað sometimes counted one hundred and twenty, the long hundred of northern trade.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 hundrað 有时指一百二十，即北方贸易中的「长百」。

items.en: Middle English kept both the counting and the district senses; the administrative sense later faded except in place names.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了计数与行政区两义，后者后来只残留在地名中。

items.en: Modern English settled on the plain number, adding the vague hundreds of and the perfect-score sense.
items.cn: 现代英语固定为单纯数词，并发展出 hundreds of 的模糊义与满分义。

note.en: The look-alike group lists related number words. The meaning group gathers other vague large-quantity markers.
note.cn: 形近组列出相关数词；词义组收集其他表示大量事物的模糊说法。

entries.definition: position 100 in a series, or one part of a hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 第一百；百分之一。由本词加序数后缀构成。

entries.definition: an old unit of weight, about fifty kilograms in Britain.
entries.definitionCN: 英担。旧重量单位，英国约合五十公斤。

entries.definition: a person who hunts. Only the letters look similar; the root is hunt.
entries.definitionCN: 猎人。只是字形相近，词根是 hunt。

entries.definition: twelve of something, or dozens of for an indefinite many.
entries.definitionCN: 一打；dozens of 表示大量。

entries.definition: the number 1,000; thousands of marks an even bigger crowd.
entries.definitionCN: 千；thousands of 表示更大量。

entries.definition: an extremely large number, originally ten thousand in Greek.
entries.definitionCN: 无数。希腊语原指一万，今为书面语的大量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks anchor hundred in counting by tens and in the family of hundredth and hundreds of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 hundred 锚定在十进制计数和 hundredth、hundreds of 词族上。

normal.en: Count ten tens: ten, twenty ... one hundred. Hundred is ten tens.
normal.cn: 十个十相加：十、二十……一百。hundred 就是十个十。

normal.en: With a number in front, no s: three hundred; alone or vague, add s: hundreds of.
normal.cn: 前面有数字不加 s：three hundred；泛指则加 s：hundreds of。

normal.en: hundredth shifts it to order or fraction: the hundredth day, one hundredth of the cost.
normal.cn: hundredth 把它变成序数或分数：第一百天、百分之一的成本。

normal.en: Old law counted people: a hundred was a district of one hundred households.
normal.cn: 古法按人计数：hundred 曾是百户行政区。

normal.en: a hundred percent means everything, not just the number on a test.
normal.cn: a hundred percent 指全部投入，不只是卷面分数。

abstract.en: One image: a full grid of one hundred little squares, every cell filled.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一百个小格子组成的大格子，每格都填满。

abstract.en: Feel the jump: ten is hands, hundred is beyond two hands, a crowd.
abstract.cn: 感受跳跃：十是双手，百超出双手，成群。

abstract.en: Treat hundred as a fence post on the number line where vague many begins.
abstract.cn: 把 hundred 当数轴上「模糊的多」开始的界桩。

examples.en: The library holds hundreds of old maps.
examples.cn: 图书馆藏有数百幅古地图。

examples.en: She ran the hundred meters in twelve seconds.
examples.cn: 她十二秒跑完一百米。

examples.en: Over two hundred guests attended the wedding.
examples.cn: 两百多位客人参加了婚礼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「汗的瑞的」：数到一百，汗都数出来了，何其多。

root: 古英语 hund「百」+ -red「计数」（日耳曼语词根），与德语 Hundert 同源；古诺斯语 hundrað 曾计一百二十，古英语中亦指百户行政区。

sensesIntro.en: Hundred begins as the exact number, then loosens into vague plenty, slices scales into order and fraction, and finally stands for the whole of a standard score.
sensesIntro.cn: hundred 从精确的数起步，松弛为泛指的大量，把刻度切成序位与分数，最终代表标准分里的全部。

core.en: A full round unit of counting, beyond which exact counting turns into vague many.
core.cn: 一个完整的整数单位，越过它精确计数就变成模糊的多。

branches.en: EXACT NUMBER: the cardinal 100, unchanged after numerals.
branches.cn: 精确数词：基数一百，跟在数字后不变。

branches.en: VAGUE MANY: hundreds of things you never bother to count.
branches.cn: 泛指大量：hundreds of，多到懒得清点。

branches.en: SCALE POSITION: place value, centuries of life, the hundredth in a series.
branches.cn: 刻度位置：数位、百年人生、系列中的第一百。

branches.en: TOTAL SCORE: a hundred percent of effort or support.
branches.cn: 满分：百分之百的努力或支持。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATION: the old hundred as a district built on a count of households.
branches.cn: 行政区：旧时以百户计数划分的 hundred 区。

intro.en: Hundred forms few derivatives, but the ordinal hundredth and the compound hundredweight are regular family members.
intro.cn: hundred 派生不多，序数词 hundredth 与复合词 hundredweight 是常规词族成员。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic, so the Latin entries section stays empty; the related numbers come from the same Germanic counting system.
latinIntro.cn: 本词族属日耳曼源，拉丁同源词一栏留空；相关数词出自同一日耳曼计数系统。

items.example: A hundred steps lead to the tower.

items.meaning: number 100 in a series; one of 100 equal parts
items.example: This is the hundredth copy printed.
Hundreds of boats fill the harbor.
The sacks were sold by the hundredweight.

items.meaningCN: 一百零一；也指琐碎细节
items.example: She gave a hundred and one excuses.
items.exampleCN: 她找了一百零一个借口。

items.example: Rates rose five per hundred.
items.exampleCN: 比率千分之五十地上升了。

items.example: The yield increased a hundredfold.
Traders once reckoned a long hundred of hides.
items.exampleCN: 商人旧时按长百计皮货。

definition_en: the feeling of needing food, or a strong desire for something
core_image: 空胃在喊叫，或心在向某物伸手
scene: 救援物资迟迟未到。The refugees were weak with hunger after days of walking.
sceneCN: 这里 hunger 是「饥饿」（第 1 个义项：缺少食物的状态）；句意：难民走了几天之后饿得虚弱无力。

derivatives.zh: 饥饿的；由名词变形容词后缀而来

senses.title: The need for food
senses.definition: the uncomfortable feeling caused by lack of food
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少食物而产生的不适感
senses.example: Hunger drove them to eat wild fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 饥饿驱使他们吃野果。
senses.why: The core bodily image is an empty stomach demanding to be filled.
senses.whyCN: 核心的身体意象是空胃在要求被填满。

senses.title: Strong desire for something
senses.definition: a very strong wish for something non-physical
senses.definitionCN: 对非物质事物的强烈愿望
senses.example: Her hunger for success never faded.
senses.exampleCN: 她对成功的渴望从未消退。
senses.why: The stomach ache is mapped onto the heart: wanting something feels like wanting food.
senses.whyCN: 胃的空虚被映射到心上：渴望某物如同渴望食物。

senses.title: Widespread shortage of food
senses.definition: a period when many people in an area do not have enough food
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区许多人吃不饱的时期
senses.example: The war brought hunger to the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 战争使整个地区陷入饥荒。
senses.why: One person's empty stomach scaled up to a whole population becomes famine.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的空胃放大到全体人群，就成了饥荒。

senses.title: To hunger for: to crave
senses.definition: to have a strong desire for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物怀有强烈渴望
senses.example: They hungered for news of home.
senses.exampleCN: 他们渴盼家乡的消息。
senses.why: The noun is turned into a verb: to feel that stomach-like pull toward something.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：像胃那样朝某物拉扯。

intro.en: Hunger comes from Old English hungor, from a Germanic root shared with hungry, the same root that gives Latin fames its cousin in other families. It has always joined the body and the heart.
intro.cn: hunger 来自古英语 hungor，出自与 hungry 同源的日耳曼词根，始终同时连着身体与心灵。

items.en: The reconstructed root *hunghuz meant to hunger; cognates appear in Dutch honger and German Hunger.
items.cn: 重构词根 *hunghuz 意为饥饿，同源词见于荷兰语 honger、德语 Hunger。

items.en: Old English hungor named both famine and appetite; the verb hungrian meant to hunger for.
items.cn: 古英语 hungor 兼指饥荒与食欲，动词 hungrian 意为渴求。

items.en: Middle English hunger kept the food sense and grew the desire sense in religious writing about hungering for righteousness.
items.cn: 中古英语保留食物义，并在宗教文本「渴慕公义」中长出渴望义。

items.en: Early modern English favored hunger as a verb of craving in sermons and poetry.
items.cn: 近代早期英语在布道文与诗歌中偏爱把 hunger 用作渴求动词。

items.en: Modern English added hunger strike in the nineteenth century, when refusing food became a political weapon.
items.cn: 现代英语在十九世纪加入 hunger strike，绝食成为政治抗争手段。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the hunger family and a false cousin. The meaning group collects words for appetite and desire.
note.cn: 形近组展示 hunger 词族与一个假表亲；词义组收集表示食欲与渴望的词。

entries.definition: feeling hunger; the adjective of this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 饥饿的。本词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: past form of the verb hunger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 hunger 的过去式。

entries.definition: a frame for hanging clothes. It looks similar but comes from hang.
entries.definitionCN: 衣架。字形相近但来自 hang。

entries.definition: the wish to eat, or a taste for something; more neutral than hunger.
entries.definitionCN: 食欲；兴趣。比 hunger 中性。

entries.definition: extreme scarcity of food over a region; stronger and more official than sense 03.
entries.definitionCN: 饥荒。比第 3 义项更重、更正式。

entries.definition: an intense, often sudden urge, especially for a specific thing.
entries.definitionCN: 渴求。常指对某样东西突如其来的强烈欲望。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie hunger to hungry, to the verb hunger for, and to the old medical idea of an empty stomach ruling the mood.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 hunger 与 hungry、动词 hunger for，以及「空胃支配心情」的旧观念连在一起。

normal.en: Drop the y: hungry minus y plus er gives hunger. The noun is the family base.
normal.cn: hungry 去掉 y 加 er 就是 hunger。名词是词族的基础。

normal.en: hunger for knowledge: your stomach-style ache is now aimed at facts.
normal.cn: hunger for knowledge：胃式的空虚转向了知识。

normal.en: hunger strike is refusing food on purpose; the word is used as a weapon.
normal.cn: hunger strike 是主动拒食，这个词被当作武器使用。

normal.en: die of hunger is the strongest fixed phrase; famine is the public-scale version.
normal.cn: die of hunger 是最重的固定说法；famine 是它的公共规模版本。

normal.en: Remember the pair: hunger is the feeling, hungry is the state.
normal.cn: 记住配对：hunger 是那种感觉，hungry 是那种状态。

abstract.en: One image: a bell inside the body rings until it is fed, by bread or by a dream.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：体内的钟一直响，直到被面包或被梦想喂饱。

abstract.en: Wanting is physical first; every mental desire borrows the stomach's language.
abstract.cn: 欲望先是身体的，一切心理渴望都借用了胃的语言。

abstract.en: Scale matters: one belly, one heart, one whole region starving.
abstract.cn: 尺度很重要：一副肠胃、一颗心、一整片挨饿的地区。

examples.en: He collapsed from hunger after three days.
examples.cn: 三天后他饿倒了。

examples.en: The child showed a real hunger to learn.
examples.cn: 这孩子表现出真正的求知渴望。

examples.en: Millions faced hunger that winter.
examples.cn: 那年冬天数百万人面临饥饿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「慌戈」：饿得发慌，拿着戈到处找吃的。

root: 古英语 hungor「饥饿」，出自日耳曼语词根 *hunghuz，与德语 Hunger、荷兰语 honger 同源；词义路径为「胃的空虚→心灵的渴望→全地区的饥荒」。

sensesIntro.en: Hunger starts in the stomach, climbs into the heart as desire for anything, widens to a region without food, and turns back into a verb for craving.
sensesIntro.cn: hunger 从胃出发，升入心中成为对一切的渴望，扩展为整片无粮之地，再折回动词表示渴求。

core.en: An emptiness inside that demands to be filled, with food or with anything.
core.cn: 内在的空虚要求被填满，用食物或用任何东西。

branches.en: BODY: the physical need for food.
branches.cn: 身体：对食物的生理需要。

branches.en: HEART: desire aimed at success, knowledge or love.
branches.cn: 心灵：指向成功、知识或爱的渴望。

branches.en: REGION: famine, hunger at the scale of a population.
branches.cn: 地区：饥荒，整个群体的饥饿。

branches.en: VERB: hungering for, the pull phrased as an action.
branches.cn: 动词：hungering for，把拉扯说成动作。

branches.en: WEAPON: the hunger strike, refusing the body's need to make a point.
branches.cn: 武器：绝食抗议，用拒绝对身体需求的满足来表达诉求。

intro.en: Hunger is a bare Germanic noun; the family adds hungry, hungered and compounds like hunger strike.
intro.cn: hunger 是光杆日耳曼名词；词族加了 hungry、hungered 及 hunger strike 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty because this word family is purely Germanic; appetite and famine come from Latin but are not related.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空，因为本词族纯出日耳曼语；appetite 与 famine 来自拉丁语但无亲缘。

items.meaning: the need for food; strong desire
items.example: Hunger gnawed at the crew.
The hungry child rubbed his eyes.
She hungered for approval.
The prisoners began a hunger strike.
They hungered for freedom.
His hungers drove him from city to city.
items.exampleCN: 种种渴望驱使他辗转各城。

items.example: The drug leaves patients hungerless.
items.exampleCN: 这种药使病人没有饥饿感。

items.example: She looked hungeringly at the display.

definition_zh: 饥饿的；渴望的；荒年的；粗劣的
definition_en: feeling hunger, or strongly wanting something
core_image: 肚子空了，眼睛却亮了
scene: 放学铃响了很久。The hungry children ran home as fast as they could.
sceneCN: 这里 hungry 是「饥饿的」（第 1 个义项：想吃东西的状态）；句意：饥饿的孩子们飞快地跑回家。

derivatives.zh: 饥饿地；形容词加副词后缀

senses.title: Needing food
senses.definition: feeling a need to eat
senses.definitionCN: 想吃东西的状态
senses.example: Skipping breakfast left him hungry all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 没吃早饭让他一上午都饿着。
senses.why: The adjective states the body condition directly: the stomach is empty.
senses.whyCN: 形容词直接陈述身体状态：胃是空的。

senses.title: Craving something non-food
senses.definition: strongly wanting something such as knowledge or success
senses.definitionCN: 强烈想要知识或成功等事物
senses.example: The young reporter was hungry for a big story.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻记者渴望拿到大新闻。
senses.why: The stomach image is lifted to ambition: appetite without bread.
senses.whyCN: 把胃的意象抬升为抱负：没有面包的胃口。

senses.title: Marked by scarcity of food
senses.definition: describing times or places where food is scarce
senses.definitionCN: 形容食物匮乏的时期或地方
senses.example: Hungry years drove families to the cities.
senses.exampleCN: 饥馑岁月迫使家庭进城。
senses.why: A person's state is spread over years and regions: hungry winters, hungry lands.
senses.whyCN: 个人的状态铺展到年月和土地：饥饿的冬天、饥饿的土地。

senses.title: Eager and greedy
senses.definition: showing intense, almost greedy interest
senses.definitionCN: 表现出近乎贪婪的强烈兴趣
senses.example: The team gave a hungry performance in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在决赛中打得如饥似渴。
senses.why: Wanting too much becomes hunger of the eyes: desire without restraint.
senses.whyCN: 想要太多就成了眼中的饥饿：不受节制的欲望。

intro.en: Hungry is Old English hungor, hunger, plus -ig, an adjective ending. It has always been the everyday word for the state that the noun names.
intro.cn: hungry 是古英语 hungor 加形容词后缀 -ig。它一直是该名词所命名状态的日常用词。

items.en: The root *hunghuz underlies Dutch hongerig and German hungrig, the same adjective family across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 词根 *hunghuz 支撑着荷兰语 hongerig、德语 hungrig，整个日耳曼语的形容词词族同源。

items.en: Old English hungri described both empty stomachs and, early on, craving hearts.
items.cn: 古英语 hungri 既形容空胃，也很早就形容渴望的心。

items.en: Middle English hungry hardened the spelling and added hungry ground for barren land.
items.cn: 中古英语定型拼写，并用 hungry ground 指贫瘠土地。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English also used hungry of lean cattle and barren fields before the metaphor settled on people.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语也用 hungry 形容瘦畜与贫田，后来比喻才落到人身上。

items.en: Modern English kept the body sense central while hungry for became a common metaphor of ambition.
items.cn: 现代英语保持身体义为核心，hungry for 则成为雄心的常用比喻。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the hunger family and one false friend. The meaning group compares words for wanting.
note.cn: 形近组收录 hunger 词族与一个假朋友；词义组比较表示「想要」的词。

entries.definition: the noun behind this adjective; the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词背后的名词；那种感觉本身。

entries.definition: in a hungry manner.
entries.definitionCN: 饥饿地。本词的副词形式。

entries.definition: feeling anger. It rhymes and ends the same way but comes from anger, not hunger.
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒的。押韵且结尾相同，但来自 anger。

entries.definition: extremely hungry, often exaggerated in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 饿极的。日常口语常作夸张用法。

entries.definition: needing water; also used metaphorically for wanting knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 口渴的。也比喻渴望知识。

entries.definition: keen and excited to do or get something, without the emptiness image.
entries.definitionCN: 热切的。积极期待，但没有空虚意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks play on the hunger-hungry pair, the hungry for metaphor and the angry trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩在 hunger-hungry 配对、hungry for 比喻与 angry 陷阱上做文章。

normal.en: hunger plus y: the noun grows a tail and becomes the adjective.
normal.cn: hunger 加 y：名词长出尾巴变成形容词。

normal.en: go hungry means to have nothing to eat at all.
normal.cn: go hungry 指完全没饭吃。

normal.en: hungry for news: your appetite has switched from rice to headlines.
normal.cn: hungry for news：胃口从米饭换成了新闻标题。

normal.en: Do not mix hungry and angry: one is the stomach, one is the temper.
normal.cn: 别把 hungry 和 angry 弄混：一个在胃里，一个在脾气里。

normal.en: Comparatives swap y for i: hungrier, hungriest.
normal.cn: 比较级把 y 换成 i：hungrier、hungriest。

abstract.en: One image: bright eyes over an empty bowl.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：空碗上方亮着的眼睛。

abstract.en: Hunger is the simplest motivation story: emptiness pushes you toward the door.
abstract.cn: 饥饿是最简单的动机故事：空虚推你走向门。

abstract.en: Feel the two directions: food comes in, ambition pulls out.
abstract.cn: 感受两个方向：食物进来，野心向外拉。

examples.en: After the match the players were hungry and tired.
examples.cn: 比赛结束后球员们又饿又累。

examples.en: She was hungry for recognition as a writer.
examples.cn: 她渴望作为作家得到认可。

examples.en: No child should go hungry at school.
examples.cn: 在学校里不该有孩子挨饿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「慌个里」：饿得心里慌个不停，肚子咕咕作响。

root: 古英语 hungor（饥饿）加形容词后缀 -ig 构成 hungry；词根为日耳曼语 *hunghuz，与德语 hungrig 同源。词义路径为「空腹→渴望→缺粮之地」。

sensesIntro.en: Hungry states the body first, then borrows that emptiness for ambition, spreads it over barren years and lands, and finally shades into greedy eagerness.
sensesIntro.cn: hungry 先说身体，再把那份空虚借给雄心，铺到贫瘠的年月与土地，最后淡入近乎贪婪的热切。

core.en: An empty stomach turned into a describing word, then lent to every kind of wanting.
core.cn: 把空胃变成一个描述词，再借给一切形式的想要。

branches.en: BODY STATE: the everyday word for needing a meal.
branches.cn: 身体状态：日常说该吃饭了的那句话。

branches.en: AMBITION: hungry for success, knowledge or news.
branches.cn: 雄心：hungry for 成功、知识或新闻。

branches.en: SCARCE LAND: hungry years and hungry soil.
branches.cn: 匮乏之地：饥饿的年月与贫瘠的土壤。

branches.en: GREED: hungry eyes that want more than they need.
branches.cn: 贪婪：想要超出所需的 hungry eyes。

branches.en: SURVIVAL: go hungry, when want becomes a real risk.
branches.cn: 生存：go hungry，匮乏变成实际危险。

intro.en: Hungry shows the common adjective ending -y attached to a noun; its family adds hungrily, hungrier and the compound half-hungry.
intro.cn: hungry 展示了名词加形容词后缀 -y 的常见构词；词族还有 hungrily、hungrier 及复合词 half-hungry。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty; this is a purely Germanic adjective family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空；这是纯日耳曼语的形容词词族。

items.example: A hungry crowd waited outside.
items.exampleCN: 饥饿的人群在外面等候。

items.example: He read the letter hungrily.
items.exampleCN: 他如饥似渴地读着那封信。

The hungriest cub ate first.

items.exampleCN: 那年冬天许多家庭挨饿。

items.exampleCN: 工人们过着半饥半饱的日子。

items.exampleCN: 这位权欲熏心的大臣很快树敌。

items.example: Hunger is the noun behind hungry.
items.exampleCN: hunger 是 hungry 背后的名词。

definition_en: to move or act faster than usual, or a need to do so
core_image: 时钟在追人跑
scene: 火车再过十分钟就要开了。We had to hurry to catch the last train.
sceneCN: 这里 hurry 是「赶快、匆忙赶路」（第 1 个义项：加快行动）；句意：我们得赶紧去赶最后一班火车。

derivatives.zh: 匆忙的；由动词过去分词转形容词
匆匆赶路的人；加表人后缀

senses.title: To move faster
senses.definition: to move quickly because time is short
senses.definitionCN: 因时间紧而快速移动
senses.example: Hurry, or we will miss the ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们赶不上渡轮。
senses.why: The clock chases the body, so the feet must speed up.
senses.whyCN: 时钟在追人，所以脚步必须加快。

senses.title: To make someone move faster
senses.definition: to push another person to act or move faster
senses.definitionCN: 促使他人加快行动
senses.example: Do not hurry the children; let them finish.
senses.exampleCN: 别催孩子，让他们做完。
senses.why: The action points outward: your own rush is imposed on another person.
senses.whyCN: 动作指向外：把自己的急迫强加给别人。

senses.title: To do something too fast
senses.definition: to do something quickly and carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 匆忙且草率地做某事
senses.example: They hurried the vote through parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 他们让表决在议会里草草通过。
senses.why: Speed borrowed from moving is lent to doing: haste damages quality.
senses.whyCN: 移动的速度转借给做事：匆忙损害质量。

senses.title: Urgent need for speed
senses.definition: a state of needing to move or act quickly
senses.definitionCN: 需要快速行动的状态
senses.example: In her hurry she dropped the keys.
senses.exampleCN: 匆忙中她把钥匙掉在了地上。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun: the rush itself, often blamed for mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 动词变名词：急迫本身，常被指为失误的原因。

intro.en: Hurry first appears in late sixteenth-century English with an unknown origin, probably imitative of quick movement. It quickly displaced older words like haste in everyday speech.
intro.cn: hurry 首见于十六世纪末英语，来源不明，可能是对急促动作的拟声。它在日常用语中很快取代了 haste 等旧词。

items.en: No secure root has been found; some suggest a rare or dialect word or an imitation of bustling sound.
items.cn: 没有可靠词根；或出自罕见方言词，或为模仿忙乱声响的造词。

items.en: Hurry is first recorded around fifteen eighty, meaning to tremble or to move noisily and fast.
items.cn: hurry 约在一五八〇年首次记录，意为颤抖或喧闹而快速地移动。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the sense settled on moving or acting fast, and hurry up became the standard command.
items.cn: 十七世纪词义固定为快速行动，hurry up 成为标准催促语。

items.en: The noun hurry grew from the verb in the same period, and in a hurry became a fixed everyday phrase.
items.cn: 名词 hurry 在同期从动词长出，in a hurry 成为固定的日常短语。

items.en: The participle hurried turned into an adjective describing careless haste, as in a hurried decision.
items.cn: 分词 hurried 转为形容词，形容草率的匆忙，如 a hurried decision。

note.en: The look-alike group lists the hurry family and one false cousin. The meaning group gathers words for speed and haste.
note.cn: 形近组列出 hurry 词族与一个假表亲；词义组收集表示速度与仓促的词。

entries.definition: done faster than is proper; the participle as adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 仓促的。分词用作形容词。

entries.definition: a violent storm. It starts the same but comes from a Spanish storm god word.
entries.definitionCN: 飓风。开头相似，但源于西班牙语的暴风神名。

entries.definition: beset or harassed. Looks like hurried but comes from harry, to raid.
entries.definitionCN: 被烦扰的。形似 hurried，但来自 harry「袭扰」。

entries.definition: quick action, often too quick; hurry is the everyday twin.
entries.definitionCN: 急速。常指过快的行动；hurry 是它的日常版。

entries.definition: to move fast or a sudden fast movement; slightly more forceful.
entries.definitionCN: 冲；赶。语气略强于 hurry。

entries.definition: a very quick short run or trip.
entries.definitionCN: 猛冲。指短促的快速跑动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the hurry up command, the in a hurry phrase and the hurried trap to fix the family together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩用 hurry up 命令、in a hurry 短语和 hurried 陷阱把词族固定在一起。

normal.en: Hurry up is the two-word command everyone knows; learn it first.
normal.cn: hurry up 是人人都懂的两个词的命令，先记它。

normal.en: in a hurry: the rush is a container you stand inside.
normal.cn: in a hurry：匆忙是一个你站在里面的容器。

normal.en: hurried looks like the past tense but is often an adjective: a hurried lunch.
normal.cn: hurried 像过去式，但常是形容词：a hurried lunch。

normal.en: no hurry tells someone to relax; hurry loses its urgency.
normal.cn: no hurry 是让人放松；hurry 的紧迫感随之消失。

normal.en: Watch the spelling: y becomes i before -ed and -es, hence hurried, hurries.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：加 -ed、-es 时 y 变 i，即 hurried、hurries。

abstract.en: One image: shoes half-tied, running out of the door.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：鞋带没系完就冲出门。

abstract.en: Hurry is time pressing on the body; haste is the same pressure without a person.
abstract.cn: hurry 是时间压在身上；haste 是无人称的同一种压力。

abstract.en: Note the cost side: hurried work is work you will redo.
abstract.cn: 注意代价的一面：仓促完成的活是要返工的。

examples.en: Sorry, I can't talk now, I'm in a hurry.
examples.cn: 抱歉，现在不能聊，我赶时间。

examples.en: She hurried across the square to the clinic.
examples.cn: 她匆匆穿过广场去诊所。

examples.en: There's no hurry; the report is due next week.
examples.cn: 不着急，报告下周才交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「哈瑞」：哈，瑞瑞快跑呀，要迟到了， hurry 一声就出发。

root: hurry 约 1580 年首见，来源不确定，一般认为是拟声造词；词义由「颤抖、喧闹疾行」固定为「赶快」，名词与形容词 hurried 均由动词派生。

sensesIntro.en: Hurry runs in three directions: the body moving fast, the voice pushing others, the work done too fast; then it freezes into a noun for the rush itself.
sensesIntro.cn: hurry 朝三个方向跑：身体加快、声音催人、事情做太快；随后凝成名词，指急迫本身。

core.en: Time pressing from behind until the body, the voice or the work speeds up.
core.cn: 时间从背后施压，直到身体、声音或事情都加速。

branches.en: SELF: moving your own feet faster.
branches.cn: 自身：让自己的脚步加快。

branches.en: OTHERS: hurrying another person along.
branches.cn: 他人：催促别人加快。

branches.en: WORK: rushing a job at the cost of quality.
branches.cn: 事情：以质量为代价赶工。

branches.en: STATE: the noun for being in a rush.
branches.cn: 状态：名词化的匆忙。

branches.en: RELIEF: no hurry, when the pressure is lifted.
branches.cn: 宽解：no hurry，压力解除时说的一句。

intro.en: Hurry carries the spelling rule of consonant plus y: before -ed and -es the y becomes i, which shapes the whole family.
intro.cn: hurry 体现了「辅音加 y」的拼写规则：加 -ed、-es 时 y 变 i，整个词族都由此塑形。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty because hurry is an English word of unknown, probably imitative origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空，hurry 是来源不明、可能为拟声的英语本族词。

items.example: Hurry, the shop closes at six.
He always hurries his breakfast.
She made a hurried exit.
Hurrying passengers filled the platform.
items.exampleCN: 匆匆赶路的乘客挤满站台。

items.example: Hurry up and finish your soup.
She left in a hurry.
They hurriedly packed their bags.

items.meaning: a person who hurries; historical coal-mine runner
items.meaningCN: 匆匆赶路者；旧时煤矿运煤童工
items.example: Hurriers pulled coal carts underground.
items.exampleCN: 运煤童工在井下拉煤车。

definition_zh: 使受伤；疼痛；伤害（感情）；损伤
definition_en: to injure a body part or cause emotional pain, or to feel painful
core_image: 碰一下就疼：身体或心里的一道口子
scene: 楼梯上有人绊了一下。She fell down the stairs and hurt her ankle.
sceneCN: 这里 hurt 是「使受伤」（第 1 个义项：造成身体损伤）；句意：她从楼梯上摔下来伤了脚踝。

senses.title: To injure the body
senses.definition: to cause injury or pain to a body part
senses.definitionCN: 使身体某处受伤或疼痛
senses.example: He hurt his back lifting the box.
senses.exampleCN: 搬箱子时他伤了背。
senses.why: The core is physical damage: contact leaves a mark that aches.
senses.whyCN: 核心是身体损伤：接触留下会疼的伤痕。

senses.title: To feel painful
senses.definition: to ache or be sore
senses.definitionCN: 发疼或酸痛
senses.example: My tooth hurts when I drink cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 喝凉水时我的牙疼。
senses.why: The verb flips direction: the body itself reports the pain.
senses.whyCN: 动词方向反转：身体自己报告疼痛。

senses.title: To wound feelings
senses.definition: to upset someone emotionally
senses.definitionCN: 在感情上使某人难过
senses.example: Her cold reply hurt him deeply.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡的回复深深伤了他。
senses.why: Pain of the skin is mapped onto the heart: words can cut without touching.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤之痛被映射到心上：言语不用触碰也能割伤。

senses.title: To damage interests
senses.definition: to harm chances, business or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 损害机会、生意或名声
senses.example: The scandal hurt the company's sales.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻损害了公司的销售。
senses.why: Damage is extended from flesh to things that cannot bleed but can weaken.
senses.whyCN: 损伤从血肉延伸到不会流血却会变弱的事物。

senses.title: Upset as an adjective
senses.definition: feeling wounded by what someone did or said
senses.definitionCN: 因他人的言行而感到受伤
senses.example: She looked hurt when nobody remembered her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 没人记得她生日时她一脸委屈。
senses.why: The past participle settles into an adjective: the wound remains visible on the face.
senses.whyCN: 过去分词沉淀为形容词：伤口仍显现在脸上。

intro.en: Hurt comes from Old French hurter, to strike or knock, first used of colliding things, then of bodies and finally of feelings. English took it in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries.
intro.cn: hurt 来自古法语 hurter「撞击」，先用于物与物相撞，再到身体，最后到感情。英语于十二三世纪借入。

items.en: Old French hurter meant to knock against or collide, of rams butting or carts hitting walls.
items.cn: 古法语 hurter 指相互碰撞，如公羊顶角、车撞墙。

items.en: The ultimate origin of hurter is uncertain; suggestions include a Frankish root for shove and a Germanic word for jostle.
items.cn: hurter 的更早来源不确定，有法兰克语「推」与日耳曼语「推挤」等假说。

items.en: Middle English hurten first meant to strike or collide, as in knights hurting each other in tournaments.
items.cn: 中古英语 hurten 先指击打或相撞，如比武大会上骑士互撞。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the sense had shifted to bodily injury and then to emotional pain.
items.cn: 十四世纪词义转向身体伤害，继而是感情之痛。

items.en: Modern English added the intransitive ache, the adjective hurt and the hurtful family.
items.cn: 现代英语加入不及物的「发疼」用法、形容词 hurt 与 hurtful 词族。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the hurt family and two dangerous look-alikes. The meaning group compares injury words for body, heart and interests.
note.cn: 形近组区分 hurt 词族与两个危险形近词；词义组比较身体、心灵与利益的受伤用词。

entries.definition: causing emotional pain; said of words and acts.
entries.definitionCN: 伤人的。形容言语与行为。

entries.definition: to move very fast, often wildly. It keeps the old Old French collision sense of the same verb family.
entries.definitionCN: 疾驰猛冲。保留了同族动词在古法语里的撞击旧义。

entries.definition: an old word for a male deer; one letter different, unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 雄鹿（旧词）。只差一个字母，无关。

entries.definition: to wound the body, especially seriously; stronger than hurt.
entries.definitionCN: 使受伤（较正式）。程度重于 hurt。

entries.definition: to give a deep injury, physical or emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 使受重创。可指身体或感情上的深创。

entries.definition: to damage health, safety or interests, not necessarily with pain.
entries.definitionCN: 损害。未必伴随疼痛感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the pain report it hurts, the feelings phrase and the irregular past form to bind the family.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩用疼痛报告 it hurts、感情短语与不规则过去式来绑定词族。

normal.en: hurt never changes form: hurt, hurt, hurt. Learn it as one shape.
normal.cn: hurt 词形不变：hurt、hurt、hurt，按一个形状记。

normal.en: My knee hurts: the body speaks for itself.
normal.cn: My knee hurts：身体自己开口说疼。

normal.en: hurt someone's feelings is the fixed way to say words caused pain.
normal.cn: hurt someone's feelings 是「说话伤了人」的固定说法。

normal.en: get hurt warns of risk: helmets exist so you do not get hurt.
normal.cn: get hurt 提示风险：戴头盔就是为了别受伤。

normal.en: unhurt is the lucky version: the crash ended and everyone was unhurt.
normal.cn: unhurt 是幸运版本：事故结束，全员无伤。

abstract.en: One image: a bruise that shows on skin and on a face.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一块淤青，显现在皮肤上，也显现在脸上。

abstract.en: Hurt is the everyday word: minor, human, repeatable, unlike wound or injure.
abstract.cn: hurt 是日常词：轻微、人性、可反复，不同于 wound、injure。

abstract.en: Pain travels: body to heart to interests, always the same verb.
abstract.cn: 疼痛会迁移：从身体到心到利益，用的都是同一个动词。

examples.en: Be careful with that knife or you will hurt yourself.
examples.cn: 小心那把刀，不然会伤到自己。

examples.en: It hurts to laugh after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后一笑就疼。

examples.en: The news of the layoffs hurt morale.
examples.cn: 裁员的消息挫伤了士气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「赫特」：磕到桌角，疼得直吸气——赫，特疼！

root: 古法语 hurter「撞击」（来源不确定，或出法兰克语系），中古英语 hurten「击打→身体受伤→伤心」，现代英语兼有动词、形容词与名词用法；过去式与过去分词同形为 hurt。

sensesIntro.en: Hurt starts as a collision, turns into bodily injury, learns to ache by itself, cuts into feelings, then weakens businesses and reputations.
sensesIntro.cn: hurt 从相撞开始，变成身体受伤，学会自己发疼，割进感情，再削弱生意与名声。

core.en: A knock that leaves a mark, on flesh, on feelings or on fortunes.
core.cn: 一次撞击留下印记：在血肉上、感情上或运气上。

branches.en: BODY: hurting an arm, a back or an ankle.
branches.cn: 身体：伤到手臂、后背或脚踝。

branches.en: ACHE: the body reporting pain by itself.
branches.cn: 自痛：身体主动报告疼痛。

branches.en: HEART: feelings hurt by words and coldness.
branches.cn: 心灵：被言语与冷淡伤到的感情。

branches.en: INTERESTS: sales, chances or reputations hurt.
branches.cn: 利益：销售、机会或名声受损。

branches.en: FACE: the visible hurt look of someone wounded inside.
branches.cn: 神色：内心受伤者脸上可见的 hurt 表情。

intro.en: Hurt keeps one form across tenses; the family adds hurtful, unhurt and compounds like hurt feelings.
intro.cn: hurt 各时态同形；词族加上 hurtful、unhurt 及 hurt feelings 之类复合语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: the word came through Old French from an uncertain Germanic source, with no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：该词经古法语传入，出自不确定的日耳曼源头，无拉丁亲缘。

items.meaning: to injure; to ache; to wound feelings
items.example: Did the fall hurt you?
The smoke hurt their eyes.
The hurt passengers waited for help.
That was a hurtful thing to say.
Amazingly, everyone walked away unhurt.
items.exampleCN: 不可思议的是，所有人安然无恙。

items.example: Old hurts healed slowly.
The hurting knee kept him awake.
It was a hurtless joke among friends.
items.exampleCN: 那只是朋友间无伤大雅的玩笑。

definition_en: the man that someone is married to, or to use resources carefully
core_image: 住在同一屋檐下、当家持户的人
scene: 婚礼上交换戒指之后。She introduced the tall man as her husband.
sceneCN: 这里 husband 是「丈夫」（第 1 个义项：结婚对象中的男性一方）；句意：她介绍那位高个子男人是她的丈夫。

derivatives.zh: 丈夫般的；善持家的；加形容词后缀
农艺；节约管理；加名词后缀

senses.title: A married man
senses.definition: the man to whom someone is married
senses.definitionCN: 某人所嫁的男性配偶
senses.example: Her husband cooks dinner every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她丈夫每周五做晚饭。
senses.why: The word names the male partner of the household bond.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名家庭纽带中的男性一方。

senses.title: To use resources frugally
senses.definition: to manage money, time or supplies carefully so they last
senses.definitionCN: 精打细算地管理钱财、时间或物资使其持久
senses.example: They husbanded their water on the long voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 长途航行中他们省着用水。
senses.why: The old housekeeping sense survives: a husband once managed the house, so husbanding means careful housekeeping of resources.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「持家」得以保留：husband 曾指管家，husbanding 便指像管家那样爱惜资源。

senses.title: To manage land or livestock
senses.definition: to cultivate or manage crops, animals or land
senses.definitionCN: 经营庄稼、牲畜或土地
senses.example: The valley has been husbanded for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷被世代经营耕种。
senses.why: Managing a household scales up to managing a farm: same careful keeping.
senses.whyCN: 管家的谨慎放大到经营农场：同样的精心守护。

senses.title: A ship's husband or householder title
senses.definition: a person who manages affairs or property for another, in old use
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中替他人管理事务或财产的人
senses.example: The ship's husband fitted out the vessel.
senses.exampleCN: 船舶经纪人负责装备这条船。
senses.why: The manager sense detached from marriage and named agents who cared for property.
senses.whyCN: 管理义脱离婚姻，指照管财产的代理人。

intro.en: Husband comes from Old Norse husbondi, house-dweller, the free owner or tenant who keeps a house. The marriage sense narrowed from the manager of a household, and the frugal verb keeps that older meaning alive.
intro.cn: husband 来自古诺斯语 husbondi「住户」，即持屋的自由业主或佃农。婚姻义由「家宅管理者」收窄而来，节俭动词则让旧义存活至今。

items.en: Old Norse husbondi joined hus, house, and bondi, dweller or farmer, one who stays and keeps the land.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 husbondi 由 hus「屋」加 bondi「居住者、农夫」构成，指留居守土之人。

items.en: Old English borrowed husbonda early for a male householder or manager of an estate.
items.cn: 古英语很早就借入 husbonda，指男性户主或庄园管事。

items.en: Middle English husband narrowed to a married man while keeping the sense of one who manages the household.
items.cn: 中古英语 husband 收窄为已婚男子，同时保留「持家者」之义。

items.en: The verb husband appeared in the fifteenth century meaning to manage thriftily, from the housekeeping image.
items.cn: 动词 husband 于十五世纪出现，意为节俭管理，源自持家意象。

items.en: Modern English added husbandry, the farming and thrift noun, and kept the rare agent senses.
items.cn: 现代英语派生 husbandry「农艺、节俭」，并保留罕见的代理人之义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the household family. The meaning group compares marriage words and the frugal verb's near neighbours.
note.cn: 形近组收录「户宅」词族；词义组比较婚姻用词与节俭动词的近邻。

entries.definition: the care and management of crops, animals or resources.
entries.definitionCN: 农艺；节约管理。本词加后缀的名词。

entries.definition: a married woman keeping the house; built from the same hus + bond idea.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭主妇。由同一 hus + bond 构词法造成。

entries.definition: an obsolete spelling still seen in old books; same word, different clothes.
entries.definitionCN: husband 的旧拼写，旧书中仍可见；同词异形。

entries.definition: a husband or wife, either partner.
entries.definitionCN: 配偶。不分性别的正式说法。

entries.definition: a person sharing a life or enterprise, married or not.
entries.definitionCN: 伴侣；合伙人。不限于婚姻。

entries.definition: to protect and save resources, close to the frugal verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 节约保护资源。接近第 2 义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into hus + band, link it to husbandry, and flag the surprise verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 hus 加 band，串起 husbandry，并标记那个出人意料的动词。

normal.en: See house + band inside husband: the one bound to the house.
normal.cn: 在 husband 里看到 house 加 band：与屋子绑在一起的人。

normal.en: husbandry hides inside husband; it means careful farming and thrift.
normal.cn: husbandry 藏在 husband 里；意为精细的农事与节俭。

normal.en: As a verb it surprises: husband your savings means spend them slowly.
normal.cn: 作动词很意外：husband your savings 指慢慢花钱。

normal.en: husband and wife is a fixed pair phrase; learn them together.
normal.cn: husband and wife 是固定配对短语，一起记。

normal.en: ex-husband adds the prefix; the house bond is untied.
normal.cn: ex-husband 加了前缀：与屋子的纽带解开了。

abstract.en: One image: a door with a man standing in it, keeping the home.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一扇门前站着守家的男人。

abstract.en: Old law called anyone who kept a house a husband; marriage borrowed the title.
abstract.cn: 旧法把持屋者都叫 husband；婚姻借用了这个头衔。

abstract.en: Frugality is housekeeping in miniature: guard the stores as you guard the door.
abstract.cn: 节俭是缩小的持家：像守门那样看守库存。

examples.en: My husband is the quiet one in our family.
examples.cn: 我丈夫是我们家安静的那位。

examples.en: The city husbanded its fuel during the cold spell.
examples.cn: 寒潮期间该市节约使用燃料。

examples.en: Good husbandry keeps the soil rich year after year.
examples.cn: 精耕细作让土壤年年保持肥沃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「哈兹笨的」：哈，自家老公有点笨笨的，但是持家可靠。

root: 古诺斯语 husbondi「住户」（hus 屋 + bondi 居住者、农夫），古英语借为 husbonda「户主」；中古英语收窄为「丈夫」，动词义「节俭管理」保留旧义的持家核心。

sensesIntro.en: Husband names the man of the house, keeps the older meaning of managing a household in the frugal verb, extends it to farms and lingers in old agent titles.
sensesIntro.cn: husband 命名一家之男，把更古老的持家义保存在节俭动词里，延伸到农场，并残留在旧职名中。

core.en: The person bound to the house: keeper first, spouse second.
core.cn: 与屋子绑在一起的人：先是守家者，后是配偶。

branches.en: SPOUSE: the modern everyday meaning.
branches.cn: 配偶：现代的日常义。

branches.en: THRIFT: husbanding money, time and supplies.
branches.cn: 节俭：爱惜钱财、时间与物资。

branches.en: LAND: husbanding fields and livestock.
branches.cn: 土地：经营田地与牲畜。

branches.en: AGENT: the old manager and ship's husband.
branches.cn: 代理人：旧时的管事与船舶经纪人。

branches.en: FAMILY: husbandry as the household art that fed the name.
branches.cn: 家业：husbandry 这门持家之术正是名字的来源。

intro.en: Husband builds a small family with husbandry, husbandly and housewife, all from the same house-keeping root.
intro.cn: husband 构成一个小词族：husbandry、husbandly、housewife，全部出自同一「持屋」词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty; the family is Norse and Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空；该词族出自诺斯语与日耳曼语，与拉丁语无关。

items.meaning: a married man; to use frugally
items.example: They husbanded every scrap of rope.
Animal husbandry was taught at the college.
Both husbands joined the school trip.
items.exampleCN: 两位丈夫都参加了学校郊游。

items.example: The colony husbanded its seed corn.
Husbanding reserves kept the firm alive.
items.exampleCN: 惜用储备让公司活了下来。

items.example: His husbandly habits kept the shop orderly.
items.exampleCN: 他持家的习惯让店铺井井有条。

items.example: The housewife ran the farm accounts.

items.meaning: an agent who outfits a ship
items.example: The ship's husband bought the new sails.
items.exampleCN: 船舶经纪人购置了新帆。

definition_en: frozen water, or to cover something with a layer of frozen water
core_image: 水在冷里站住不动了
scene: 冬天清晨的湖边一步一滑。The lake was covered with thin ice.
sceneCN: 这里 ice 是「冰」（第 1 个义项：水冻结成的固体）；句意：湖面覆盖着薄冰。

derivatives.zh: 冰冷的；多冰的；加形容词后缀

senses.title: Frozen water
senses.definition: water that has frozen hard
senses.definitionCN: 水冻结成的坚硬固体
senses.example: The pond froze and the children slid on the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘结冰，孩子们在冰上滑行。
senses.why: Cold stops water from moving; the stopping itself becomes a thing you can touch.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷让水停止流动，这种「停住」本身成了可以触摸的东西。

senses.title: Ice cream or iced drinks
senses.definition: a frozen sweet dessert, or drinks served very cold
senses.definitionCN: 冰冻甜点或加冰的饮品
senses.example: Two cones of ice, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请来两个冰淇淋蛋筒。
senses.why: The frozen water is sweetened and served: the substance becomes a treat.
senses.whyCN: 冰冻的水加糖上桌：物质变成了甜点。

senses.title: A cold manner
senses.definition: coldness in a person's manner or welcome
senses.definitionCN: 态度或接待中的冷淡
senses.example: Her answer was delivered with ice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答带着冷冰冰的腔调。
senses.why: Physical coldness maps onto emotional distance: a chill you can feel in a voice.
senses.whyCN: 身体的冷映射到情感的距离：语气里能感到寒意。

senses.title: To freeze or chill
senses.definition: to cover with ice, to chill, or to coat with icing
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖冰层、冰镇或涂糖霜
senses.example: The roads iced over during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里路面结了冰。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: ice acts on things, on drinks and even on cakes.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词：冰作用于物体、饮料甚至蛋糕。

senses.title: Diamonds in slang
senses.definition: diamonds, in informal slang
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指钻石
senses.example: The rapper wore ice on every finger.
senses.exampleCN: 那个说唱歌手每根手指都戴着钻石。
senses.why: Diamonds sparkle cold and clear, so slang borrowed the frozen stone image.
senses.whyCN: 钻石冷冽清澈，俚语便借用了这块「冻住的石头」的意象。

intro.en: Ice is an Old English word, is or isen, of Germanic origin, related to Old High German is. Its root beyond Germanic is uncertain, but the word has never left English everyday speech.
intro.cn: ice 是古英语词 is 或 isen，属日耳曼源，与古高地德语 is 同源；日耳曼之外的词根不确定，但它从未离开过英语日常用语。

items.en: The Germanic root gives Dutch ijs and German Eis; the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根给出荷兰语 ijs、德语 Eis；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English is meant ice; the compound isen, to make of ice, appears in early texts.
items.cn: 古英语 is 指冰；复合形式 isen「用冰制作」见于早期文本。

items.en: Middle English is grew compounds like is-bred, ice-bright, in poetry.
items.cn: 中古英语 is 在诗歌中长出 is-bred「冰亮」等复合词。

items.en: Modern English spelled it ice and built the family: icy, iceberg, ice cream.
items.cn: 现代英语定拼为 ice，构建词族：icy、iceberg、ice cream。

items.en: The verb ice and the slang sense for diamonds grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 动词 ice 与指钻石的俚语义在十九二十世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the ice family and one false friend. The meaning group compares cold words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 ice 词族与一个假朋友；词义组比较表示寒冷的词。

entries.definition: very cold or covered with ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰冷的。本词的形容词。

entries.definition: the passage between seats. It sounds the same but means a walkway.
entries.definitionCN: 过道。发音相同，却指座位间的通道。

entries.definition: a huge floating mass of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰山。ice 加 berg 的复合词。

entries.definition: thin frozen moisture on surfaces, not a solid sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 霜。表面的薄冰晶，不是整块冰。

entries.definition: soft frozen flakes falling from the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 雪。天上落下的软冰晶。

entries.definition: hard pellets of ice falling during storms.
entries.definitionCN: 冰雹。暴风雨中落下的冰粒。

normalIntro.en: These hooks play on the sound of aisle, the break the ice idiom and the icy family.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用与 aisle 的同音、break the ice 惯用语及 icy 词族。

normal.en: ice sounds like aisle but means frozen water; picture the letter i standing on ice.
normal.cn: ice 与 aisle 同音，但指冻住的水；想象字母 i 站在冰上。

normal.en: break the ice: the first joke cracks the frozen silence.
normal.cn: break the ice：第一个笑话敲裂了冻结的沉默。

normal.en: icy turns the noun cold and slippery.
normal.cn: icy 把名词变得又冷又滑。

normal.en: on ice means stored or postponed; put the plan on ice.
normal.cn: on ice 指封存或暂缓；put the plan on ice。

normal.en: Slang ice means diamonds: the coldest sparkle.
normal.cn: 俚语 ice 指钻石：最冷的闪光。

abstract.en: One image: a glass of water gone still and hard overnight.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一夜之间那杯水静止变硬。

abstract.en: Ice is water with time stopped inside it.
abstract.cn: 冰是内部时间被冻结的水。

abstract.en: Feel the range: a drink, a pond, a stare, a diamond.
abstract.cn: 感受范围：一杯饮料、一个池塘、一个眼神、一颗钻石。

examples.en: The bartender dropped an ice cube into the glass.
examples.cn: 调酒师往杯里放了一块冰。

examples.en: She skated across the frozen ice.
examples.cn: 她滑过冻结的冰面。

examples.en: The winter storm iced the power lines.
examples.cn: 冬季风暴让电线结了冰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱死」：夏天爱死冰淇淋里的那块冰了。

root: 古英语 is「冰」，日耳曼语词根，与荷兰语 ijs、德语 Eis 同源；更深来源不确定。现代英语派生 icy、iceberg 等，动词与俚语义为近代发展。

sensesIntro.en: Ice is frozen water first, then a frozen treat, then the chill in a manner, a verb of freezing and chilling, and slang for diamonds.
sensesIntro.cn: ice 先是冻住的水，再是冰冻的甜点、态度里的寒意、冻结与冰镇的动词，最后是钻石的俚语。

core.en: Water stopped by cold, made into something you can touch and feel.
core.cn: 被寒冷停住的水，变成可触摸可感知之物。

branches.en: WATER SOLID: the pond, the cube, the sheet.
branches.cn: 固态水：池塘、冰块、冰面。

branches.en: TREAT: ice cream and iced drinks.
branches.cn: 甜点：冰淇淋与加冰饮料。

branches.en: MANNER: a greeting served with ice.
branches.cn: 态度：冷冰冰的接待。

branches.en: ACTION: roads iced over, cakes iced white.
branches.cn: 动作：路面结冰、蛋糕敷上白霜。

branches.en: JEWELS: slang ice for diamonds.
branches.cn: 珠宝：俚语 ice 指钻石。

intro.en: Ice builds a wide compound family: iceberg, ice cream, ice cube, and the adjective icy with its adverb and noun.
intro.cn: ice 构成庞大的复合词族：iceberg、ice cream、ice cube，以及形容词 icy 及其副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty; the family is Germanic, and Latin glacies is an unrelated word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空；该词族属日耳曼语，拉丁语 glacies 并无亲缘。

items.example: The path was sheeted with ice.
Icy winds swept the coast.
She replied icily.
There was an iciness in his tone.
Only a tip of the iceberg shows.

items.meaning: a ship or remark that breaks ice or silence
items.example: The teacher opened with an icebreaker.
Iced coffee sells well in summer.

items.meaning: sweet coating on cakes; the forming of ice
items.example: The cake was covered in white icing.

definition_en: a thought, plan or suggestion formed in the mind
core_image: 脑子里亮起的一盏小灯
scene: 会议室安静了很久。Then he raised his hand and offered a new idea.
sceneCN: 这里 idea 是「主意」（第 1 个义项：脑中形成的计划或提议）；句意：他举手提出了一个新主意。

derivatives.zh: 构思；形成概念；动词化形式

senses.title: A plan or suggestion
senses.definition: a plan or suggestion offered in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情境中提出的计划或建议
senses.example: Her idea saved the school trip.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主意挽救了学校郊游。
senses.why: A lamp lights up in the head: something actionable appears.
senses.whyCN: 脑中亮起一盏灯：可付诸行动的东西出现了。

senses.title: A mental picture or concept
senses.definition: a thought or image held in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 心中持有的想法或图像
senses.example: The idea of freedom means different things to different people.
senses.exampleCN: 自由的概念因人而异。
senses.why: The light need not act; it can simply illuminate a notion.
senses.whyCN: 这盏灯不必行动，它也可以只照亮一个概念。

senses.title: Vague knowledge or belief
senses.definition: a rough knowledge or opinion about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的大致认识或看法
senses.example: I have no idea where the keys went.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全不知道钥匙去哪了。
senses.why: The mind holds a shadow of a thing: enough to guess, not enough to know.
senses.whyCN: 心中持有事物的影子：够猜测，不够确知。

senses.title: The aim or point of something
senses.definition: the purpose or point behind an action or design
senses.definitionCN: 行动或设计背后的目的
senses.example: The idea of the game is to work together.
senses.exampleCN: 这个游戏的本意是协作。
senses.why: The idea becomes the plan's inner intention, not a thought in a head.
senses.whyCN: idea 变成计划内在的意图，而非头脑中的念头。

senses.title: High conception in philosophy
senses.definition: in philosophy, a timeless archetype or perfect form
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中超越时间的原型或完美形式
senses.example: Plato placed eternal ideas above the world of things.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图把永恒理念置于万物之上。
senses.why: The everyday thought is raised to a perfect, eternal model.
senses.whyCN: 日常的想法被提升为完美永恒的范型。

intro.en: Idea comes from Greek idea, look or form, the verb idein, to see. Plato made it a technical term for eternal forms, and Latin and the European languages inherited it.
intro.cn: idea 源自希腊语 idea「外观、形式」，出自动词 idein「看」。柏拉图将其定为指永恒理念的术语，拉丁语及欧洲诸语言继承了它。

items.en: Greek idea meant form, pattern or look, from idein, to see; what is seen with the mind's eye.
items.cn: 希腊语 idea 意为形式、样式或外观，出自 idein「看」；即心灵之眼所见之物。

items.en: Plato used idea for the eternal, perfect models behind visible things.
items.cn: 柏拉图用 idea 指可见事物背后永恒完美的范型。

items.en: Latin borrowed idea as a learned word and kept it in philosophical writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语将 idea 作为学术词借入，保存在哲学写作中。

items.en: Middle English took idea through Latin in the sixteenth century, first in Platonic contexts.
items.cn: 中古英语经拉丁语在十六世纪借入 idea，最初用于柏拉图式语境。

items.en: Modern English loosened the term until any thought or plan could be an idea.
items.cn: 现代英语放宽词义，任何想法或计划都可称 idea。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the idea family. The meaning group compares thought words from a quick spark to a formal concept.
note.cn: 形近组收录 idea 词族；词义组比较从灵光一闪到正式概念的思考用词。

entries.definition: a perfect model or standard; also, existing only in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 理想；理想的。同根的姊妹词。

entries.definition: a system of ideas behind politics or culture.
entries.definitionCN: 意识形态。理念的系统化。

entries.definition: an object of worship. Sounds close but comes from a Greek word for image in a religious sense.
entries.definitionCN: 偶像。发音相近，但出自希腊语「宗教形象」一词。

entries.definition: anything produced by thinking; broader than idea.
entries.definitionCN: 想法。范围比 idea 宽。

entries.definition: a vague or personal belief or concept.
entries.definitionCN: 观念。较含糊、较个人化。

entries.definition: an abstract general idea, often in academic use.
entries.definitionCN: 概念。偏抽象、常用于学术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split idea into i + dea, play on the seeing root, and use the no idea phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 idea 拆成 i 加 dea，玩味「看」的词根，并用 no idea 短语。

normal.en: The root means to see: an idea is what your inner eye sees.
normal.cn: 词根意为「看」：idea 是心眼所见。

normal.en: no idea is the everyday negative: I have no idea at all.
normal.cn: no idea 是日常否定式：我毫无头绪。

normal.en: a bright idea is the lightbulb cartoon moment.
normal.cn: a bright idea 就是漫画里灯泡亮起的瞬间。

normal.en: ideal is idea plus al: the perfect version of a thought.
normal.cn: ideal 是 idea 加 al：想法的完美版。

normal.en: get ideas warns that someone is dreaming above their place.
normal.cn: get ideas 警示有人开始想入非非。

abstract.en: One image: a small lamp switching on in a dark head.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：黑暗的头颅里小灯亮起。

abstract.en: An idea is a seed: small, complete, ready to grow.
abstract.cn: idea 是种子：小而完整，随时可以生长。

abstract.en: From spark to system: idea, ideal, ideology.
abstract.cn: 从火花到体系：idea、ideal、ideology。

examples.en: That's a great idea; let's try it this weekend.
examples.cn: 这主意太好了，周末就试试。

examples.en: The idea behind the design is simplicity.
examples.cn: 这个设计背后的理念是简约。

examples.en: Nobody had any idea how hard the climb would be.
examples.cn: 没人知道这次攀登有多艰难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱地里挖」：好主意就像埋在地里的宝贝，爱到地里挖才挖得出来。

root: 希腊语 idea「形式、外观」（idein「看」），柏拉图用以指永恒理念；经拉丁语于十六世纪进入英语，现代英语放宽为任何想法、主意。

sensesIntro.en: Idea runs from a doable plan to a mental image, a vague belief, the inner purpose of a design, and finally the perfect forms of philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: idea 从可执行的主意到心中图像、模糊的印象、设计的本意，最终抵达哲学中的完美理念。

core.en: A light switched on inside the mind: something seen before it exists.
core.cn: 头脑里亮起的一盏灯：事物存在之前先被看见。

branches.en: PROPOSAL: an idea you can act on this afternoon.
branches.cn: 提议：下午就能动手的 idea。

branches.en: CONCEPT: the idea of freedom or justice.
branches.cn: 概念：自由或正义的 idea。

branches.en: IMPRESSION: no idea, half an idea.
branches.cn: 印象：毫无头绪或略知一二。

branches.en: PURPOSE: the idea of the game or of the law.
branches.cn: 本意：游戏或法律的 idea。

branches.en: PLATONIC FORM: ideas as eternal models.
branches.cn: 柏拉图式理念：作为永恒范型的 ideas。

intro.en: Idea spawns ideal, ideology and ideate, all keeping the seeing root inside.
intro.cn: idea 派生出 ideal、ideology、ideate，都保留着「看」的词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the borrowed philosophical noun as it passed into learned European use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示这个借入的哲学名词如何进入欧洲学术用法。

items.example: She turned a rough idea into a business.
items.exampleCN: 她把粗略的想法做成了生意。

items.example: The resort matched their ideal of a holiday.
items.exampleCN: 这个度假村符合他们对假期的理想。

items.example: The party's ideology shaped its policies.
items.exampleCN: 该党的意识形态塑造了其政策。

items.example: Designers ideate before they sketch.
items.exampleCN: 设计师先构思再画草图。

items.example: His idealism outlasted the hard years.
items.exampleCN: 他的理想主义熬过了艰难岁月。

items.example: People idealize their childhood.
The committee sat idealess for hours.
items.exampleCN: 委员会枯坐数小时无计可施。

items.example: Brainstorming aids ideation.

definition_zh: 如果；是否；假如；即使（让步）
definition_en: used to introduce a condition, a doubt or an indirect question
core_image: 站在岔路口说：先看另一边会怎样
scene: 妈妈望着窗外的乌云。If it rains, we will move the picnic indoors.
sceneCN: 这里 if 是「如果」（第 1 个义项：引导条件从句）；句意：如果下雨，我们就把野餐挪到室内。

derivatives.zh: 当且仅当（数学用语）；缩合形式

senses.title: Introducing a condition
senses.definition: used to say that one thing depends on another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一事取决于另一事
senses.example: If you finish early, call me.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你提前做完，给我打电话。
senses.why: The word opens a fork in the road: what happens depends on which branch is real.
senses.whyCN: 这个词打开岔路口：结果取决于哪条岔路成真。

senses.title: Introducing an indirect question
senses.definition: used after verbs like ask or wonder, meaning whether
senses.definitionCN: 用于 ask、wonder 等动词后，意为是否
senses.example: She asked if the shop was open.
senses.exampleCN: 她问商店开没开门。
senses.why: The fork becomes a genuine question: either answer may be true.
senses.whyCN: 岔路变成真正的疑问：两种答案都可能为真。

senses.title: Concession: even if
senses.definition: used to say something is true regardless of the condition
senses.definitionCN: 表示无论条件如何某事都成立
senses.example: Even if it costs more, we will buy it.
senses.exampleCN: 即使更贵，我们也会买。
senses.why: Both forks lead to the same place: the result does not change.
senses.whyCN: 两条岔路通向同一处：结果不变。

senses.title: Wish or regret: if only
senses.titleCN: 愿望与遗憾：要是……就好了
senses.definition: used to express a strong wish about an unreal situation
senses.definitionCN: 表达对不真实情境的强烈愿望
senses.example: If only I had studied harder.
senses.exampleCN: 要是当初更用功就好了。
senses.why: The speaker stares at the road not taken and aches for it.
senses.whyCN: 说话者凝望着那条没走的路，为之怅然。

senses.title: Although or as if in comparisons
senses.definition: in as if, describing how something appears or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 在 as if 中描述事物呈现的样子
senses.example: He talked as if he owned the place.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话好像他是这里的主人。
senses.why: One road is imagined as a mirror of the real one.
senses.whyCN: 一条岔路被想象成现实道路的镜像。

intro.en: If comes from Old English gif, of Germanic origin, related to Old High German ibu and Old Norse ef. It may descend from a particle meaning so that or even so, but the deeper root is uncertain.
intro.cn: if 来自古英语 gif，属日耳曼源，与古高地德语 ibu、古诺斯语 ef 相关；或出自意指「以便、即便如此」的小词，更深词根不确定。

items.en: The Germanic family gives Old Norse ef and Old High German ibu alongside Old English gif.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族给出古诺斯语 ef 与古高地德语 ibu，与古英语 gif 并列。

items.en: Old English gif already covered conditions, doubts and concessions in law codes and poetry.
items.cn: 古英语 gif 在法典与诗歌中已涵盖条件、疑问与让步用法。

items.en: Middle English if standardized in spelling and fixed the indirect-question use after ask and know.
items.cn: 中古英语统一拼写 if，固定了 ask、know 后接间接疑问的用法。

items.en: Early modern English added the unreal wish if only and the concessive even if.
items.cn: 近代英语加入虚拟愿望 if only 与让步 even if。

items.en: Modern English built compounds and phrases: what-if, iffy, as if.
items.cn: 现代英语构成复合词与短语：what-if、iffy、as if。

note.en: The look-alike group lists short conditional words. The meaning group compares other ways of opening a condition or doubt.
note.cn: 形近组列出短小的条件词；词义组比较其他引出条件或疑问的方式。

entries.definition: uncertain or doubtful; an adjective built from if.
entries.definitionCN: 不确定的。由 if 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: a preposition. Two letters apart but no relation.
entries.definitionCN: 介词。只差一个字母，毫无关系。

entries.definition: a negative condition word, meaning if not.
entries.definitionCN: 除非。表否定条件。

entries.definition: used for indirect questions and choices; more formal than if.
entries.definitionCN: 是否。间接疑问中比 if 更正式。

entries.definition: introducing a condition, often a restriction.
entries.definitionCN: 以……为条件。常带限制意味。

entries.definition: in inverted conditionals like should you need help.
entries.definitionCN: 在倒装条件句中表假设，如 should you need help。

normalIntro.en: These hooks lean on the fork-in-the-road image, the fixed phrases and the little traps around of and whether.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩依托岔路口意象、固定短语，以及 of 与 whether 的易混陷阱。

normal.en: if is a fork in the road: first picture both branches.
normal.cn: if 是岔路口：先想象两条岔路。

normal.en: if only stares at the road not taken.
normal.cn: if only 凝望着那条没走的路。

normal.en: even if closes the fork: both roads lead to the same result.
normal.cn: even if 关闭岔路：两条路通向同一结果。

normal.en: Do not confuse if and of; only one opens a condition.
normal.cn: 别混淆 if 和 of；只有一个能打开条件。

normal.en: After ask and wonder, if can mean whether.
normal.cn: 在 ask、wonder 后，if 可以表「是否」。

abstract.en: One image: a signpost with two blank arrows.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一块立着两支空白箭头的路牌。

abstract.en: If is the smallest word that builds whole alternate worlds.
abstract.cn: if 是最小的词，却能搭建整个平行世界。

abstract.en: Grammar feels the fork: real conditions use present tense, dreams use were.
abstract.cn: 语法感受岔路：真实条件用现在时，梦想用 were。

examples.en: If you need help, just raise your hand.
examples.cn: 如果需要帮助，举手就好。

examples.en: I wonder if the museum closes on Mondays.
examples.cn: 不知道博物馆周一闭不闭馆。

examples.en: If only the weather had been kinder.
examples.cn: 要是天气再好一点就好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一分」：如果考试多一分，我就能进决赛——一切从「如果」开始。

root: 古英语 gif「如果」，日耳曼语源，与古诺斯语 ef、古高地德语 ibu 同族；更深词根不确定。派生形容词 iffy 及复合词 what-if 为后世发展。

sensesIntro.en: If opens roads: a real condition, an indirect doubt, a concession that closes the fork, a wish for the road not taken, and an imagined mirror of reality.
sensesIntro.cn: if 打开道路：真实条件、间接疑问、关闭岔路的让步、对未走之路的愿望，以及对现实的想象镜像。

core.en: A fork opened in speech: reality may take either branch.
core.cn: 在语言中打开的岔路口：现实可以走任意一条岔路。

branches.en: CONDITION: if you finish early.
branches.cn: 条件：如果你提前完成。

branches.en: DOUBT: asked if the shop was open.
branches.cn: 疑问：问商店是否开门。

branches.en: CONCESSION: even if it costs more.
branches.cn: 让步：即使更贵。

branches.en: WISH: if only I had studied.
branches.cn: 愿望：要是当初学过就好了。

branches.en: APPEARANCE: as if he owned the place.
branches.cn: 仿佛：as if 他是这里的主人。

intro.en: If builds few descendants, but iffy, what-if and the set phrases carry the little word far.
intro.cn: if 的后代不多，但 iffy、what-if 及各种固定短语让这个小词走得很远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: if is a Germanic function word with no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：if 是日耳曼语功能词，与拉丁语无亲缘。

items.example: If the door is locked, knock twice.
The deal is still iffy.
If only we had left earlier.
items.exampleCN: 要是我们早点出发就好了。

items.example: She smiled as if nothing happened.
items.exampleCN: 她微笑着，仿佛什么都没发生。

items.example: Even if it rains, we go.
The plan covers every what-if.
items.exampleCN: 该计划覆盖了各种假设情形。

items.example: The proof holds iff the matrix is square.
items.exampleCN: 仅当矩阵为方阵时证明成立。

items.example: Will you come? If so, reply today.
items.exampleCN: 你会来吗？如果来，今天回复。

definition_zh: 有病的；不健康的；坏的；恶劣的；有害地
definition_en: not healthy, bad or harmful, or badly
core_image: 脸色发白地躺着；事情往坏里走
scene: 教室里有张座位空着。He stayed home because he felt ill.
sceneCN: 这里 ill 是「有病的」（第 1 个义项：身体不舒服）；句意：他因为感觉生病而待在家里。

pos.zh: 恶行；不幸；the ills：种种弊病

senses.title: Sick and unwell
senses.definition: suffering from sickness or poor health
senses.definitionCN: 遭受疾病或健康不佳
senses.example: The baby fell ill during the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿在旅途中病倒了。
senses.why: The word paints a body gone pale and weak.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描绘一副苍白虚弱的身体。

senses.title: Bad or unfavorable
senses.definition: bad in quality or bringing harm
senses.definitionCN: 质量差或带来损害
senses.example: The plan met with ill luck from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这计划从一开始就运气不佳。
senses.why: Sickness is a bad state, so the word widens to anything bad.
senses.whyCN: 生病是坏状态，词义便扩展到一切坏事。

senses.title: Hostile or unfriendly
senses.definition: showing hostility or bad intent
senses.definitionCN: 表现出敌意或坏心思
senses.example: He bore no ill feeling toward the judge.
senses.exampleCN: 他对法官并无恶意。
senses.why: A bad heart is the illness of feelings.
senses.whyCN: 坏心肠是情感的病。

senses.title: Badly, in an adverbial way
senses.definition: badly or poorly, in set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 在固定短语中表示差、糟
senses.example: The proposal was ill received.
senses.exampleCN: 该提案反响恶劣。
senses.why: The adjective bends into the adverb: done in a bad way.
senses.whyCN: 形容词弯成副词：以糟糕的方式做成。

senses.title: Social problems as ills
senses.definition: problems or evils in society
senses.definitionCN: 社会中的问题或弊病
senses.example: Poverty and crime are the ills of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困与犯罪是这座城市的弊病。
senses.why: Bad states collected together become named evils.
senses.whyCN: 各种坏状态集合起来，就成了有名目的恶。

intro.en: Ill comes from Old Norse illr, bad, borrowed into northern Middle English where it pushed aside the older sick in many uses. The Norse source itself is of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: ill 来自古诺斯语 illr「坏」，借入北部中古英语，在许多用法中排挤了旧词 sick；诺斯语源头本身来源不确定。

items.en: Old Norse illr meant bad, evil or hard; its ultimate root is uncertain.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 illr 意为坏的、恶的、艰难的；其更早词根不确定。

items.en: Middle English ill entered through the north and first meant bad in a general way.
items.cn: 中古英语 ill 经北方进入，最初泛指坏。

items.en: By the fifteenth century ill was common for sickness, especially in northern usage.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，ill 已常用于疾病，尤见于北方用法。

items.en: Modern English split the register: ill for serious sickness and set phrases, sick for everyday vomiting and American illness.
items.cn: 现代英语分化语域：ill 指重病与固定短语，sick 指日常病态与美式用法。

items.en: The adverbial and noun uses solidified in phrases like ill advised and the ills of society.
items.cn: 副词与名词用法在 ill advised、the ills of society 等短语中固化。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the ill family and close spellings. The meaning group compares sickness and badness words.
note.cn: 形近组区分 ill 词族与相近拼写；词义组比较疾病与恶劣用词。

entries.definition: the state of being ill; a disease.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病。本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: illegal or forbidden. Starts the same but comes from Latin licere, to be allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 非法的。开头相同，但源自拉丁语 licere「被允许」。

entries.definition: a raised area of land; one letter changes everything.
entries.definitionCN: 小山。一个字母之差，意义全变。

entries.definition: unwell; in American English the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 生病的。美式英语的日常用词。

entries.definition: in poor health, in a gentle polite way.
entries.definitionCN: 欠安。委婉礼貌的说法。

entries.definition: often ill and weak-looking.
entries.definitionCN: 多病的。常病且显得虚弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the fall ill phrase, the worse-worst comparison and the ill will collocation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用 fall ill 短语、worse-worst 比较级链和 ill will 搭配。

normal.en: fall ill is the standard way to become sick in formal English.
normal.cn: fall ill 是正式英语里「生病」的标准说法。

normal.en: ill has no own comparatives: ill, worse, worst.
normal.cn: ill 没有自己的比较级：ill、worse、worst。

normal.en: ill will is a bad heart made into a phrase.
normal.cn: ill will 把坏心肠固定成短语。

normal.en: speak ill of means to badmouth; the adverb hides in it.
normal.cn: speak ill of 指说坏话；副词藏在其中。

normal.en: ill-fated joins ill to fate: a doomed journey from the start.
normal.cn: ill-fated 把 ill 接到 fate 上：从一开始就注定失败。

abstract.en: One image: a pale face and a turned-down mouth.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：苍白的脸和向下撇的嘴。

abstract.en: Ill travels from body to luck to heart to society.
abstract.cn: ill 从身体游走到运气、人心乃至社会。

abstract.en: Register matters: doctors write ill, friends say sick.
abstract.cn: 语域很重要：医生写 ill，朋友说 sick。

examples.en: She has been ill for two weeks.
examples.cn: 她病了两周了。

examples.en: The bridge was an ill-designed structure.
examples.cn: 这座桥是个设计恶劣的结构。

examples.en: No ill feeling remained after the talk.
examples.cn: 会谈之后再无恶意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一偶」：一偶感风寒，人就 ill 了。

root: 古诺斯语 illr「坏」（来源不确定），经北部中古英语借入；词义路径为「坏→有病的→恶意的→副词恶劣地→名词社会弊病」；比较级用 worse、worst。

sensesIntro.en: Ill starts as plain badness, settles on sickness, turns hostile, bends into an adverb, and collects into the noun ills for society's evils.
sensesIntro.cn: ill 从单纯的坏出发，落定于疾病，转向敌意，弯成副词，最后聚合成指社会之恶的名词 ills。

core.en: Something gone wrong: in a body, a plan, a heart or a city.
core.cn: 出了岔子的东西：身体、计划、内心或城市。

branches.en: HEALTH: ill health, fall ill.
branches.cn: 健康：ill health、fall ill。

branches.en: QUALITY: ill luck, ill-fated.
branches.cn: 品质：ill luck、ill-fated。

branches.en: HEART: ill will, ill feeling.
branches.cn: 人心：ill will、ill feeling。

branches.en: MANNER: ill received, ill advised.
branches.cn: 方式：ill received、ill advised。

branches.en: SOCIETY: the ills of poverty and crime.
branches.cn: 社会：贫困与犯罪之弊。

intro.en: Ill compounds freely: illness, ill-fated, illiterate-lookalikes and the classic ill will.
intro.cn: ill 构词自由：illness、ill-fated、形近的 illiterate 系，以及经典的 ill will。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: ill is a Norse loan, unrelated to Latin malus or the prefix in-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：ill 是诺斯语借词，与拉丁语 malus 及前缀 in- 无关。

items.example: The crew fell ill on the voyage.
Illness kept him out of school.
The book lists the ills of modern work.
items.exampleCN: 这本书列举现代职场的弊病。

items.example: The ill-fated expedition lost its ships.
items.exampleCN: 这次厄运缠身的远征失去了船只。

items.example: He left without ill will.
Many were illiterate then.
It was an ill-advised promise.
He had an illness-free winter.

definition_en: a sickness, or the state of being ill
core_image: 从健康到卧床之间的一段路
scene: 秋天的流感季节。A sudden illness kept the captain ashore.
sceneCN: 这里 illness 是「疾病」（第 1 个义项：具体的病症或患病状态）；句意：一场突发的疾病让船长留在了岸上。

derivatives.zh: 有病的；名词的形容词基础

senses.title: A sickness or disease
senses.definition: a condition of bad health; a disease
senses.definitionCN: 健康状况不佳的状态；疾病
senses.example: He caught an illness on the ship.
senses.exampleCN: 他在船上得了病。
senses.why: The name covers any state of being unwell, from colds to worse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词涵盖任何不健康的状态，从感冒到更重的病。

senses.title: The period of being ill
senses.definition: the time during which someone is ill
senses.definitionCN: 某人患病的时段
senses.example: Her illness lasted the whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她的病缠绵了整个冬天。
senses.why: The condition stretches into time: an illness with a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 状态延伸为时间：一场有起点也有终点的病。

senses.title: Mental sickness
senses.definition: a disorder of the mind rather than the body
senses.definitionCN: 心灵的而非身体的失调
senses.example: Treatments for mental illness have improved.
senses.exampleCN: 精神疾病的治疗已有改进。
senses.why: The word reaches the mind as well as the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个词同样触及心灵。

senses.title: Weakness of a group or system
senses.definition: a state of weakness or trouble in a system or society
senses.definitionCN: 系统或社会陷入虚弱或麻烦的状态
senses.example: Corruption is an illness of the state.
senses.exampleCN: 腐败是国家肌体的疾病。
senses.why: Bodily sickness becomes a picture of failing institutions.
senses.whyCN: 身体的病成了运转失灵体制的画像。

intro.en: Illness is ill plus -ness, the state suffix. The pair fixed itself in English in the fifteenth century as ill, borrowed from Old Norse, spread south.
intro.cn: illness 由 ill 加状态后缀 -ness 构成。十五世纪，随着诺斯语借词 ill 向南传播，这一组合在英语中定型。

items.en: The base ill comes from Old Norse illr, bad.
items.cn: 词基 ill 来自古诺斯语 illr「坏」。

items.en: Middle English added the suffix -nesse to ill, first meaning badness in general.
items.cn: 中古英语给 ill 加后缀 -nesse，最初泛指恶劣。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the word leaned toward sickness and poor health.
items.cn: 至十五世纪，词义偏向疾病与不健康。

items.en: Modern English separated illness from disease: illness is the patient's state, disease the named condition.
items.cn: 现代英语将 illness 与 disease 分开：illness 指病人的状态，disease 指有名称的病症。

items.en: The nineteenth and twentieth centuries added mental illness and public-health usage.
items.cn: 十九二十世纪加入 mental illness 与公共卫生用法。

note.en: The look-alike group lists sickness nouns. The meaning group separates the patient's state from the named disease.
note.cn: 形近组列出疾病类名词；词义组区分病人状态与病名。

entries.definition: plural; several sicknesses.
entries.definitionCN: 复数；多种疾病。

entries.definition: readiness to do something. Same -ness tail, opposite mood.
entries.definitionCN: 乐意。相同的 -ness 尾巴，情绪相反。

entries.definition: the state of being sick; parallel word from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 患病状态。来自另一词根的平行词。

entries.definition: a named medical condition, often specific.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病。指有名称的具体病症。

entries.definition: a minor, often chronic complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 小恙。轻微且常为慢性的不适。

entries.definition: a disease or serious social problem.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病；弊病。书面语，兼指社会问题。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split illness into ill + ness, contrast it with disease and reuse the recover-from phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 illness 拆成 ill 加 ness，与 disease 对比，并复用 recover from 短语。

normal.en: ill + ness = the state of being ill; the suffix packs it into a noun.
normal.cn: ill 加 ness ＝ 患病状态；后缀把它打包成名词。

normal.en: illness is your state; disease is its name. Flu is a disease that causes illness.
normal.cn: illness 是你的状态，disease 是它的名称。流感是造成不适的 disease。

normal.en: recover from an illness: the road out of the state.
normal.cn: recover from an illness：走出这种状态的路。

normal.en: mental illness speaks of the mind, not the body.
normal.cn: mental illness 说的是心灵而非身体。

normal.en: a long illness stretches time; a sudden illness strikes at once.
normal.cn: a long illness 拉长时间；a sudden illness 一下子袭来。

abstract.en: One image: a bed with a calendar on the wall.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一张床，墙上挂着日历。

abstract.en: Illness is a tunnel: it has an entrance and, usually, an exit.
abstract.cn: illness 是一条隧道：有入口，通常也有出口。

abstract.en: Note the pairing: ill the adjective, illness the noun, both short and pale.
abstract.cn: 注意配对：形容词 ill，名词 illness，都短而苍白。

examples.en: The illness spread quickly through the crew.
examples.cn: 疾病在船员中迅速蔓延。

examples.en: He never fully recovered from that illness.
examples.cn: 他始终未能从那场病中完全康复。
