examples.en: Mental illness should be treated with care.
examples.cn: 精神疾病应当得到细心治疗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「依耦呢斯」：病中总依偎着枕头呢，说的是生病的状态。

root: illness = 古诺斯语借词 ill「坏」+ 状态后缀 -ness；十五世纪定型为「疾病、患病状态」；现代英语与 disease 分工：illness 重状态，disease 重病名。

sensesIntro.en: Illness names a sickness, stretches into the time of being ill, reaches the mind, and finally portraits failing institutions as a sick body.
sensesIntro.cn: illness 命名疾病，延伸为患病时段，触及心灵，最终把失灵的体制描绘成病体。

core.en: The state of a body or mind gone wrong, packed into one noun.
core.cn: 身体或心灵出了问题的一种状态，打包成一个名词。

branches.en: DISEASE STATE: catching an illness.
branches.cn: 病症：得了一场 illness。

branches.en: PERIOD: an illness lasting all winter.
branches.cn: 病程：缠绵整个冬天的 illness。

branches.en: MIND: mental illness and its care.
branches.cn: 心灵：mental illness 及其治疗。

branches.en: BODY POLITIC: an illness of the state.
branches.cn: 国家肌体：国家的 illness。

branches.en: RECOVERY ROAD: recovering from an illness.
branches.cn: 康复之路：从 illness 中恢复。

intro.en: Illness is a transparent build: the adjective ill plus the state suffix -ness, alongside siblings like kindness and weakness.
intro.cn: illness 构词透明：形容词 ill 加状态后缀 -ness，与 kindness、weakness 等同族词并列。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: the word is Norse plus an English suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：该词由诺斯语词基加英语后缀构成。

items.meaning: a sickness; the state of being ill
items.example: Her illness began in March.
The ill patient needed rest.
The hospital treats many illnesses.
items.exampleCN: 这家医院治疗多种疾病。

items.example: Mental illness carries no shame.
An illness-free year at last.
Seasickness is a common sickness.
Illness left a weakness in his legs.
items.exampleCN: 疾病给他的腿留下乏力。

items.example: Wellness is the opposite of illness.
items.exampleCN: wellness 是 illness 的反面。

definition_en: to form a picture or idea of something in the mind
core_image: 在脑内放映一场不存在的电影
scene: 孩子们的教室里。Imagine you are sailors on a windy sea.
sceneCN: 这里 imagine 是「想象、设想」（第 1 个义项：在脑中构建图景）；句意：想象你们是狂风大作的海上的水手。

derivatives.zh: 虚构的；假想的；加形容词后缀

senses.title: To picture in the mind
senses.definition: to form a mental image of something not present
senses.definitionCN: 为不在眼前的事物在心中形成图像
senses.example: Close your eyes and imagine the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 闭上眼睛想象那片海滩。
senses.why: The mind projects a scene onto its dark screen.
senses.whyCN: 心灵把一幕场景投射到自己的暗幕上。

senses.title: To suppose or believe
senses.definition: to assume or believe something to be true
senses.definitionCN: 假定或认为某事属实
senses.example: I imagine he forgot the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜他忘了开会。
senses.why: The mental picture hardens into a tentative belief.
senses.whyCN: 心中的图像凝固成初步的判断。

senses.title: To invent something unreal
senses.definition: to create something that does not exist
senses.definitionCN: 创造出不存在的东西
senses.example: The author imagined a city under the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 作者虚构了一座海底之城。
senses.why: The projector is set free: it makes worlds that were never filmed.
senses.whyCN: 放映机被放开：它造出从未被拍摄的世界。

senses.title: To conceive a possibility
senses.definition: to think of something as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把某事设想为可能
senses.example: Imagine winning the prize twice.
senses.exampleCN: 设想两次赢得这个奖。
senses.why: The mind rehearses an outcome before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 心灵在结果发生前先进行彩排。

senses.title: To wrongly believe
senses.definition: to believe wrongly that something is happening
senses.definitionCN: 错误地相信某事正在发生
senses.example: You imagined the footsteps; the street was empty.
senses.exampleCN: 脚步声是你幻听，街上空无一人。
senses.why: The projector runs without light: false pictures feel real.
senses.whyCN: 放映机在无光时运转：虚假的图像也显得真实。

intro.en: Imagine comes from Latin imaginari, to picture to oneself, from imago, an image or copy. French imagine carried it into English, keeping the picture at the heart of the word.
intro.cn: imagine 来自拉丁语 imaginari「在心中成像」，词基 imago「影像、摹本」。法语 imagine 把它带入英语，词心始终是「图像」。

items.en: Latin imago meant a copy, portrait or mental image; the ancestor of English image.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 指摹本、肖像或心中影像；是英语 image 的祖先。

items.en: The verb imaginari meant to form such images in the mind.
items.cn: 动词 imaginari 意为在心中形成这类影像。

items.en: Old French imaginer passed the verb to medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 imaginer 把该动词传给中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English imagine at first meant to form a mental picture, then to devise a plan.
items.cn: 中古英语 imagine 先指在心中成像，继而指谋划。

items.en: Modern English built imagination, imaginary and imaginative around it.
items.cn: 现代英语围绕它构建 imagination、imaginary 与 imaginative。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the image family and two confusing neighbors. The meaning group compares thinking verbs.
note.cn: 形近组收录 image 词族与两个易混邻词；词义组比较思考类动词。

entries.definition: the power or act of imagining.
entries.definitionCN: 想象力。本词加后缀的名词。

entries.definition: existing only in the imagination.
entries.definitionCN: 虚构的。只存在于想象中。

entries.definition: showing creativity; describes people and ideas, not unreal things.
entries.definitionCN: 有创意的。形容人与想法，不指虚幻之物。

entries.definition: to visualize, usually more concretely than imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 设想。通常比 imagine 更具体。

entries.definition: to assume without proof, close to sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 假定。接近第 2 义项。

entries.definition: to imagine while asleep or wistfully awake.
entries.definitionCN: 做梦；遐想。睡中或怅然醒时的想象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split imagine into image + ine, reuse just imagine, and warn about the imaginary-imaginative trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 imagine 拆成 image 加 ine，复用 just imagine，并警示 imaginary 与 imaginative 之辨。

normal.en: See image inside imagine: to imagine is to paint an image in your head.
normal.cn: 在 imagine 里看到 image：想象就是脑内作画。

normal.en: just imagine opens a daydream: just imagine living on the moon.
normal.cn: just imagine 开启一段白日梦：就想想住在月球上。

normal.en: I imagine takes guesses: I imagine he is late.
normal.cn: I imagine 承载猜测：我猜他迟到了。

normal.en: imaginary things do not exist; imaginative people create.
normal.cn: imaginary 的东西不存在；imaginative 的人有创造力。

normal.en: Spelling trap: no a before g in imagine, unlike the noun image plus ine.
normal.cn: 拼写陷阱：imagine 中 g 前没有 a，与名词 image 加 ine 不同。

abstract.en: One image: a small cinema behind the eyes.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：眼睛后面的小电影院。

abstract.en: Imagining is practicing reality before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象是现实到来前的彩排。

abstract.en: Careful: the projector sometimes runs without the light of truth.
abstract.cn: 小心：放映机有时在没有真相之光时运转。

examples.en: Imagine living a hundred years from now.
examples.cn: 想象一下生活在百年之后。

examples.en: I imagine the trip will take six hours.
examples.cn: 我猜这趟旅程要六个小时。

examples.en: She imagined a machine that could fly long before one existed.
examples.cn: 早在飞机出现之前她就设想了会飞的机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一摸镜」：伸手一摸镜子，镜中世界全靠想象。

root: 拉丁语 imago「影像」→ imaginari「心中成像」→ 古法语 imaginer → 中古英语 imagine；词义从成像扩展到猜想、虚构与幻听。

sensesIntro.en: Imagine projects pictures, hardens them into guesses, builds unreal worlds, rehearses futures, and sometimes runs falsely.
sensesIntro.cn: imagine 投射图像，把图像凝成猜测，搭建虚幻世界，彩排未来，有时还会虚假运转。

core.en: The mind's projector: images shown before or beyond reality.
core.cn: 心灵的放映机：在现实之前或之外放映影像。

branches.en: PICTURE: imagine the beach at sunset.
branches.cn: 图像：想象日落时分的海滩。

branches.en: SUPPOSITION: I imagine he is late.
branches.cn: 猜想：我猜他迟到了。

branches.en: INVENTION: a city imagined under the sea.
branches.cn: 虚构：设想的 underwater 城市。

branches.en: PROSPECT: imagine winning twice.
branches.cn: 设想：想象两次夺奖。

branches.en: ILLUSION: footsteps you imagined in the empty street.
branches.cn: 幻觉：空街上幻听到的脚步声。

intro.en: Imagine keeps its Latin image at the center; the family adds imagination, imaginary, imaginative and the simpler image.
intro.cn: imagine 的中心始终是拉丁语「影像」；词族加上 imagination、imaginary、imaginative 与更简的 image。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the noun imago and the verb imaginari that fed the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示 imago 名词与 imaginari 动词，整个词族由此而来。

items.example: Imagine a door in this wall.

items.meaning: the power of forming mental images
items.example: Her imagination filled the empty room.
items.exampleCN: 她的想象力填满了空屋。

items.example: The dragon is an imaginary friend.
items.exampleCN: 那条龙是个虚构的朋友。

items.example: An imaginative solution saved the day.
items.exampleCN: 富有想象力的方案扭转了局面。

items.example: The screen showed a sharp image.
The imagined threat never came.
items.exampleCN: 想象中的威胁从未到来。

items.example: The speed was unimaginable.
The book collects her early imaginings.
items.exampleCN: 此书收录了她早期的想象之作。

latinEntries.meaning: to form an image in the mind

definition_zh: 立即；马上；直接地；紧接地
definition_en: at once, without delay, or directly next to something
core_image: 零秒等待：话音未落，行动已开始
scene: 火警铃声突然响起。The students immediately left the classroom.
sceneCN: 这里 immediately 是「立即」（第 1 个义项：毫不拖延地）；句意：学生们立刻离开了教室。

derivatives.zh: 立即的；直接的；形容词基础
即时性；直接性；加名词后缀

senses.title: At once, without delay
senses.definition: without any delay
senses.definitionCN: 毫不拖延地
senses.example: Please call me immediately.
senses.exampleCN: 请立即给我打电话。
senses.why: The gap between event and response shrinks to nothing.
senses.whyCN: 事件与反应之间的间隙缩为零。

senses.title: Directly next to
senses.definition: directly beside or next to, with nothing in between
senses.definitionCN: 紧邻或紧接，中间没有间隔
senses.example: The cottage sits immediately behind the church.
senses.exampleCN: 小屋就在教堂后面紧邻处。
senses.why: The zero gap is spatial: no room lies between two things.
senses.whyCN: 零间隙变成空间的：两物之间没有任何距离。

senses.title: As a conjunction: as soon as
senses.definition: as soon as, in chiefly British use
senses.definitionCN: 主要用于英式英语，意为「一……就」
senses.example: I left immediately the meeting ended.
senses.exampleCN: 会议一结束我就走了。
senses.why: Two events are welded together: the second starts with the first.
senses.whyCN: 两件事被焊在一起：第二件随第一件开始。

senses.title: In the nearest degree of relation
senses.definition: in the closest degree of connection, as with family
senses.definitionCN: 在最紧密的关系层面，如直系亲属
senses.example: Only his immediate family knew the truth.
senses.exampleCN: 只有他的直系亲属知道真相。
senses.why: The zero gap applies to bonds: closest first, no middleman.
senses.whyCN: 零间隙适用于关系：最近者优先，无中间环节。

intro.en: Immediately builds on immediate, from Latin immmediare with the negating prefix in-, to leave nothing in between. The adverb carries both the time sense and the contact sense.
intro.cn: immediately 建立在 immediate 之上，出自拉丁语 immmediare 加否定前缀 in-，意为「中间不留任何东西」。副词兼有时间和接触两义。

items.en: Latin in- plus immediare, to act on something directly, gave immediatus, with nothing intervening.
items.cn: 拉丁语 in- 加 immediare「直接作用于某物」，给出 immediatus「无间隔」。

items.en: The negative prefix in- turned the idea into nothing-in-between.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 把这一概念变成「中间无一物」。

items.en: Late Middle English borrowed immediate in the spatial and relational senses.
items.cn: 中古英语晚期借入 immediate，取空间与关系二义。

items.en: The time sense of immediate and immediately grew strong in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: immediate 与 immediately 的时间义在十七世纪壮大。

items.en: British English added the conjunction use, immediately meaning as soon as.
items.cn: 英式英语加入连词用法，immediately 意为 as soon as。

note.en: The look-alike group lists the immediate family and a near-spelled word. The meaning group compares speed words.
note.cn: 形近组列出 immediate 词族与一个近形词；词义组比较速度类词。

entries.definition: happening at once or with nothing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 立即的；直接的。本词的形容词。

entries.definition: an obsolete spelling seen in early texts.
entries.definitionCN: 早期文本中的旧拼写。

entries.definition: extremely large. It starts the same but comes from a Latin word for measure.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的。开头相同，但源于拉丁语「测量」一词。

entries.definition: at once; emphasizes the instant itself.
entries.definitionCN: 即刻。强调瞬间本身。

entries.definition: at once, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 马上。口语说法。

entries.definition: immediately; also means simultaneously.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻；也可指同时。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into im + mediate, play on the zero-gap idea and use the conjunction trick.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 im 加 mediate，玩味零间隙概念，并用连词技巧。

normal.en: im + mediately: no middle step is kept between cause and effect.
normal.cn: im 加 mediate：因果之间不留中间步骤。

normal.en: immediately after fixes the position sense: right behind.
normal.cn: immediately after 固定位置义：紧随其后。

normal.en: In British English you can say: I left immediately it ended.
normal.cn: 英式英语可以说：I left immediately it ended。

normal.en: immediate family is the zero-gap circle of relatives.
normal.cn: immediate family 是零间隙的亲属圈。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with immense; one is speed, one is size.
normal.cn: 别和 immense 混淆：一个关于速度，一个关于尺寸。

abstract.en: One image: a hand pressing a button and the light blinking on.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：手按下按钮，灯即刻亮起。

abstract.en: Immediately is time with the waiting taken out.
abstract.cn: immediately 是抽掉等待的时间。

abstract.en: Same zero works in space: no gap between two neighbors.
abstract.cn: 同一个零也用于空间：相邻者之间没有间隙。

examples.en: The doctor came immediately after the call.
examples.cn: 电话一打完医生就来了。

examples.en: He lives immediately opposite the station.
examples.cn: 他就住在车站正对面。

examples.en: Firefighters responded immediately.
examples.cn: 消防员立即出动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一密德里特里」：一秒都不密积等待，德你立刻特里去办。

root: 拉丁语 in-（否定）+ immediare「直接作用」→ immediatus「无间隔」→ immediate「立即的、紧邻的」→ immediately；时间零间隙与空间零间隙同源。

sensesIntro.en: Immediately removes the gap: in time it means at once, in space it means next to, in grammar it welds two events, and in relationships it means closest.
sensesIntro.cn: immediately 消除间隙：时间为「马上」，空间为「紧邻」，语法中焊接两件事，关系上指最亲近。

core.en: Nothing in between: zero gap of time, space, grammar or blood.
core.cn: 中间无一物：时间、空间、语法或血缘上的零间隙。

branches.en: TIME: call me immediately.
branches.cn: 时间：immediately 给我打电话。

branches.en: SPACE: immediately behind the church.
branches.cn: 空间：教堂后紧邻处。

branches.en: SEQUENCE: left immediately it ended.
branches.cn: 先后：一结束就走。

branches.en: RELATION: immediate family.
branches.cn: 关系：直系亲属。

branches.en: POSITION: immediately opposite the station.
branches.cn: 方位：车站正对面。

intro.en: Immediately carries the negative prefix im- over mediate; the family adds immediate, immediacy and mediacy-contrast words.
intro.cn: immediately 在 mediate 上叠加否定前缀 im-；词族加上 immediate、immediacy 及与 mediacy 对照的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the verb of direct action behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示词族背后的「直接作用」动词。

items.example: Reply immediately, please.
The immediate cause was a spark.
The film's immediacy moved the audience.
items.exampleCN: 影片的现场感打动了观众。

items.example: She mediated the dispute.
An intermediate level class.
The immediateness of the danger was clear.
The immediately-adjacent lots share a wall.
items.exampleCN: 紧邻的地块共用一堵墙。

items.example: The case went to mediation.

definition_en: the quality of being important, or the state of having great value or influence
core_image: 秤上压弯指针的一块重物
scene: 校长在广播里强调安全。The headmaster stressed the importance of wearing helmets.
sceneCN: 这里 importance 是「重要性」（第 1 个义项：价值或影响的程度）；句意：校长强调佩戴头盔的重要性。

senses.title: The quality of mattering
senses.definition: the degree to which something matters or has value
senses.definitionCN: 某事物有价值或有影响的程度
senses.example: She understands the importance of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她明白睡眠的重要性。
senses.why: The scale weighs things: some press the needle hard.
senses.whyCN: 秤在称量事物：有些东西把指针压得很重。

senses.title: Consequence or influence
senses.definition: having power to affect outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 具有影响结果的力量
senses.example: A minister spoke with quiet importance.
senses.exampleCN: 部长说话带着不张扬的威望。
senses.why: What weighs heavily can move people and events.
senses.whyCN: 分量重的东西能推动人与事。

senses.title: A prominent social position
senses.definition: high rank or social standing
senses.definitionCN: 高位或显赫的社会地位
senses.example: The city grew in wealth and importance.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市在财富与地位上崛起。
senses.why: The weight of a name lifts its owner above the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 名字的分量把主人抬到人群之上。

senses.title: Exaggerated self-regard
senses.definition: an exaggerated sense of one's own worth
senses.definitionCN: 对自身价值的夸大感受
senses.example: His self-importance annoyed the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我膨胀让团队恼火。
senses.why: The scale tips toward oneself: weight claimed, not earned.
senses.whyCN: 秤盘偏向自己：宣称的重量，而非挣来的。

intro.en: Importance comes from Latin importare, to carry in or to signify, with the sense of a thing bringing its weight with it. Old French and English import and importance developed the meaning of significance.
intro.cn: importance 来自拉丁语 importare「带入、意味着」，含事物自带分量之义。古法语与英语的 import、importance 发展出「意义、重要性」的含义。

items.en: Latin importare joined in-, in, and portare, to carry: to carry in, then to mean or signify.
items.cn: 拉丁语 importare 由 in「入」加 portare「携带」构成：带入，继而指意味、表明。

items.en: Medieval Latin importantia named the significance or weight of a thing.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 importantia 指事物的意义或分量。

items.en: Old French importer carried the verb into French with the signifying sense.
items.cn: 古法语 importer 以「表明」义把动词传入法语。

items.en: Middle English import meant to convey or signify; importance followed in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 import 意为传达、表明；importance 于十五世纪随之出现。

items.en: Modern English settled the value sense and added self-importance in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 现代英语固定价值义，并于十八世纪加入 self-importance。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the import family and a false cousin. The meaning group compares weight and significance words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 import 词族与一个假表亲；词义组比较表示分量与意义的词。

entries.definition: having great value or influence.
entries.definitionCN: 重要的。本词的形容词。

entries.definition: to bring in goods; also, the meaning of a text.
entries.definitionCN: 进口；含义。同根双义词。

entries.definition: lacking power. Starts the same but comes from a Latin word for power, not carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 无力的。开头相同，但源自拉丁语「权力」一词。

entries.definition: the quality of having meaning or consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 意义；重要性。偏指意味与后果。

entries.definition: importance or influence, used metaphorically.
entries.definitionCN: 分量。比喻用法指重要性。

entries.definition: fame or notice; standing out.
entries.definitionCN: 显要。指引人注目、地位突出。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split importance into import + ance, contrast importance and importance-self, and reuse of great importance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 importance 拆成 import 加 ance，对照 self-importance，并复用 of great importance。

normal.en: import + ance: what a thing carries in is its importance.
normal.cn: import 加 ance：事物带来的东西就是它的重要性。

normal.en: attach importance to is the fixed verb pattern for valuing something.
normal.cn: attach importance to 是「重视某事」的固定动词句型。

normal.en: self-importance is weight claimed without a scale.
normal.cn: self-importance 是未经称量就自报的重量。

normal.en: importance is the noun; important is the adjective; do not swap them.
normal.cn: importance 是名词，important 是形容词，不要互换。

normal.en: A matter of no importance carries no weight at all.
normal.cn: a matter of no importance 毫无分量。

abstract.en: One image: a tiny key outweighing a mountain of junk.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一把小钥匙压过一座垃圾山。

abstract.en: Importance is influence per unit of size.
abstract.cn: 重要性是单位体积的影响力。

abstract.en: Beware the mirror: importance felt is not importance measured.
abstract.cn: 当心镜子：感觉到的重要性不等于量出的重要性。

examples.en: Teachers stress the importance of reading aloud.
examples.cn: 老师们强调朗读的重要性。

examples.en: The port lost its importance after the war.
examples.cn: 战后该港失去了重要地位。

examples.en: He spoke with the importance of a general.
examples.cn: 他带着将军般的威望说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一破腾斯」：一把重物把秤盘压破腾起，说明它太重要。

root: 拉丁语 importare「带入、表明」（in 入 + portare 携带）→ 中世纪拉丁语 importantia「分量、意义」→ 古法语 → 中古英语 importance「重要性、显要」。

sensesIntro.en: Importance measures how much a thing carries: its value, its influence, its social weight, and the false weight of self-regard.
sensesIntro.cn: importance 衡量事物的承载量：价值、影响力、社会分量，以及自我膨胀的假重量。

core.en: The weight a thing brings in with it, felt on the scale of events.
core.cn: 事物随之带入的分量，在事件的秤上被感知。

branches.en: VALUE: the importance of sleep or study.
branches.cn: 价值：睡眠或学习的重要性。

branches.en: INFLUENCE: speaking with quiet importance.
branches.cn: 影响：带着不张扬的威望说话。

branches.en: RANK: a city rising in importance.
branches.cn: 地位：一座城市的崛起。

branches.en: VANITY: self-importance without earned weight.
branches.cn: 虚荣：未经挣得的自我重要感。

branches.en: ASSESSMENT: attaching importance to what matters.
branches.cn: 评估：重视真正要紧的事。

intro.en: Importance is import plus -ance; the family adds important, importantly and the compound self-importance.
intro.cn: importance 由 import 加 -ance 构成；词族加上 important、importantly 与复合词 self-importance。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the carrying verb that split into trade goods and significance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示那个分裂为「货物进口」与「意义分量」的携带动词。

items.example: The importance of the match drew huge crowds.
items.exampleCN: 这场比赛的重要性吸引了大批观众。

items.example: This is an important notice.
More importantly, stay calm.

items.meaning: to bring in goods; to mean
items.example: They import tea from Asia.
The error seemed unimportant at first.
items.exampleCN: 起初这错误看似无关紧要。

items.example: Shake off that self-importance.
This is the importantest rule in dialect speech.
The importation of rice rose.

definition_zh: 不可能的；办不到的；难以忍受的；难对付的人或事
definition_en: not possible, or very difficult and annoying
core_image: 推一堵不会动的大门
scene: 短跑赛道的尽头线。Breaking the ten-second wall seemed impossible.
sceneCN: 这里 impossible 是「不可能的」（第 1 个义项：无法发生或完成）；句意：突破十秒这道墙似乎是不可能的。

senses.title: Cannot happen or be done
senses.definition: not able to happen, exist or be done
senses.definitionCN: 无法发生、存在或被完成
senses.example: It is impossible to be in two places at once.
senses.exampleCN: 人不可能同时出现在两地。
senses.why: The door has no handle on this side: no action opens it.
senses.whyCN: 这扇门在这一侧没有把手：任何行动都打不开。

senses.title: Too difficult to accept or bear
senses.definition: very hard to endure or deal with
senses.definitionCN: 极难忍受或应付
senses.example: The heat made the tent impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 高温让帐篷实在待不下去。
senses.why: The wall of impossibility now presses on patience, not physics.
senses.whyCN: 不可能之墙此刻压向耐心，而非物理。

senses.title: Extremely difficult to deal with
senses.definition: very difficult or annoying as a person or task
senses.definitionCN: 作为人或事极难应付
senses.example: Her uncle is an impossible guest.
senses.exampleCN: 她叔叔是个难缠的客人。
senses.why: A person can be a locked door too.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是一扇打不开的门。

senses.title: Contradicting the facts
senses.titleCN: 与事实矛盾而站不住的
senses.definition: so inconsistent that it cannot be true
senses.definitionCN: 矛盾到不可能为真
senses.example: Both reports cannot be true; that is impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告不可能都属实。
senses.why: Two truths that clash cancel each other out.
senses.whyCN: 两个互斥的真相会互相抵消。

intro.en: Impossible joins the Latin negating prefix in-, here im-, with possibilis, able to be done, from posse, to be able. It entered English through Old French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: impossible 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（此处作 im-）加 possibilis「可做到的」（词基 posse「能够」）构成，十四世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin posse meant to be able; the participle possibilis meant capable of happening.
items.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为能够；分词 possibilis 指可能发生的。

items.en: The negative prefix in- turned it into impossibilis, not able to be.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 将其变为 impossibilis「不可能的」。

items.en: Old French impossible carried the word into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语 impossible 把该词带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: Middle English impossible first described things that could not happen.
items.cn: 中古英语 impossible 先指不可能发生之事。

items.en: Modern English extended it to unbearable people and situations, and coined impossibility and impossibly.
items.cn: 现代英语扩展到难忍的人与处境，并造出 impossibility 与 impossibly。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the possible family and a sound-alike word. The meaning group compares impossibility words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 possible 词族与一个近音词；词义组比较表示不可能的词。

entries.definition: a thing that may happen; the opposite direction of the same scale.
entries.definitionCN: 可能性。同一标尺的反方向。

entries.definition: that cannot be traveled through. Sounds close; it comes from pass, not posse.
entries.definitionCN: 不可通行的。发音相近，但词基是 pass。

entries.definition: in an impossible manner or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 不可能地；难以置信地。

entries.definition: not practical to do, though perhaps possible.
entries.definitionCN: 不可行的。或许可能但不实际。

entries.definition: not allowed or worth discussing at all.
entries.definitionCN: 不予考虑。根本不值得讨论。

entries.definition: too shocking or unlikely to be considered.
entries.definitionCN: 难以想象的。令人震惊而不敢考虑。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into im + possible, use the door image and warn about impassable.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 im 加 possible，利用门意象，并警示 impassable。

normal.en: im + possible: put im- in front and the possible turns away.
normal.cn: im 加 possible：加上 im- 前缀，可能就转身离开。

normal.en: nothing is impossible is the favorite motivational phrase.
normal.cn: nothing is impossible 是最流行的励志语。

normal.en: next to impossible keeps a hair of hope: almost, but not quite.
normal.cn: next to impossible 还留有一丝希望：几乎，但不是绝对。

normal.en: an impossible guest is a locked door at dinner.
normal.cn: an impossible guest 是餐桌上一扇打不开的门。

normal.en: Do not mix impossible and impassable: one is doing, one is passing.
normal.cn: 别混淆 impossible 与 impassable：一个关于做，一个关于通行。

abstract.en: One image: a door with no handle on your side.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一扇在你这一侧没有把手的门。

abstract.en: Impossible is a verdict, not a mood: it says the world says no.
abstract.cn: impossible 是判定而非情绪：它说世界说了不。

abstract.en: Use it in three grades: unlikely, impossible, unbearable.
abstract.cn: 分三档使用：不太可能、不可能、难以忍受。

examples.en: It is impossible to fit ten people in this car.
examples.cn: 十个人塞进这辆车是不可能的。

examples.en: Without a map, finding the cabin was next to impossible.
examples.cn: 没有地图，找到小屋几乎不可能。

examples.en: The manager faced an impossible choice between staff and budget.
examples.cn: 经理面临人员与预算之间无解的抉择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一姆坡森布」：一个死脑筋硬坡上森严堡垒，当然不可能。

root: 拉丁语 posse「能够」→ possibilis「可做到的」+ 否定前缀 in-/im- → impossibilis → 古法语 impossible → 英语 impossible；引申出难忍、难缠与自相矛盾诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Impossible closes doors: of events, of patience, of temper and of truth.
sensesIntro.cn: impossible 关上四种门：事件的门、耐心的门、脾气的门、真相的门。

core.en: A door with no handle on your side: no action can open it.
core.cn: 一扇在你这一侧没有把手的门：任何行动都打不开。

branches.en: EVENT: it cannot happen or be done.
branches.cn: 事件：不可能发生或做到。

branches.en: PATIENCE: the situation is impossible to bear.
branches.cn: 耐心：处境难以忍受。

branches.en: TEMPER: an impossible person.
branches.cn: 脾气：难相处的人。

branches.en: TRUTH: claims that cannot both be true.
branches.cn: 真相：不可能同时为真的主张。

branches.en: SCALE: from next to impossible to nothing is impossible.
branches.cn: 标尺：从 next to impossible 到 nothing is impossible。

intro.en: Impossible is the negative twin of possible; the family adds impossibility, impossibly and the near-twin impassable.
intro.cn: impossible 是 possible 的否定孪生词；词族加上 impossibility、impossibly 与近孪词 impassable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the ability verb and its negated participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示能力动词及其否定分词。

items.example: An impossible task for one afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 一个下午不可能完成的任务。

items.example: They proved the impossibility of the route.
items.exampleCN: 他们证明了那条路线不可行。

items.example: The tower was impossibly tall.
A possible solution exists.
The road was impassable in snow.
We kept the possibility open.
The ledger listed impossibles.
Possibly the train was delayed.

definition_zh: 使印象深刻；使钦佩；盖印；铭刻
definition_en: to make someone feel admiration, or to press or stamp something onto a surface
core_image: 一枚印章压进蜡面留下痕迹
scene: 面试官看着桌上的模型。The candidate's handmade model impressed everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 impress 是「使印象深刻、使钦佩」（第 1 个义项：产生赞赏的效果）；句意：应聘者手工制作的模型让在场每个人都印象深刻。

derivatives.zh: 令人赞叹的；加形容词后缀
被打动的；分词转形容词

senses.title: To fill with admiration
senses.definition: to make someone feel admiration or respect
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生钦佩或敬意
senses.example: Her calm reply impressed the judges.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉着的回答令评委印象深刻。
senses.why: The stamp presses admiration into the mind as ink presses a seal.
senses.whyCN: 印章把钦佩压进脑海，如同印模压出图纹。

senses.title: To press or stamp
senses.definition: to press a mark or design onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面压出印记或图案
senses.example: The clerk impressed the seal on the certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在证书上盖了印章。
senses.why: The literal act: hard contact leaves a copy of itself.
senses.whyCN: 字面动作：坚硬的接触留下自身的复制品。

senses.title: To fix firmly in the mind
senses.definition: to make an idea stay firmly in someone's mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某个想法牢牢留在心中
senses.example: The coach impressed discipline on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让纪律深植全队心中。
senses.why: The seal is applied to memory: the mark will not wipe away.
senses.whyCN: 印章盖在记忆上：痕迹擦不掉。

senses.title: To use as a show
senses.definition: to perform in order to win admiration, often insincerely
senses.definitionCN: 为赢得赞赏而表现，常不真诚
senses.example: He bought the car just to impress the neighbors.
senses.exampleCN: 他买车只是为了给邻居留下深刻印象。
senses.why: The stamp is forged: admiration aimed at appearance, not truth.
senses.whyCN: 印章是伪造的：针对表象而非真相的钦佩。

senses.title: To compel by force (historic impressment)
senses.definition: to force someone into service, as sailors were impressed
senses.definitionCN: 强迫某人服役，如旧时强征水手
senses.example: The navy impressed young men into service.
senses.exampleCN: 海军强征年轻人入伍。
senses.why: The same pressing, applied to bodies instead of wax.
senses.whyCN: 同样的按压，从蜡面换成对人的强压。

intro.en: Impress comes from Latin imprimere, to press in or upon, from in- and premere, to press. The seal image explains every sense: pressing leaves a mark, and marks persuade.
intro.cn: impress 来自拉丁语 imprimere「压入」，由 in- 加 premere「压」构成。印章意象解释一切义项：按压留下痕迹，而痕迹能说服人。

items.en: Latin premere meant to press; imprimere meant to press into or upon something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为压；imprimere 意为压入或压上。

items.en: The noun impressio named the mark left by pressing, in wax or in the mind.
items.cn: 名词 impressio 指按压留下的痕迹，或在蜡上，或在心里。

items.en: Old French empirer and later English borrowings kept the literal stamping.
items.cn: 古法语与后来的英语借词保留了字面的盖章义。

items.en: Middle English impress meant to stamp, then to fix in the mind.
items.cn: 中古英语 impress 先指盖章，继而指铭刻于心。

items.en: The admiration sense grew strong in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; impressment named the forced naval recruitment.
items.cn: 钦佩义在十八九世纪壮大；impressment 则指强征水手。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the impress family and the historic impressment. The meaning group compares admiration and stamping words.
note.cn: 形近组区分 impress 词族与历史词 impressment；词义组比较钦佩与盖印类词。

entries.definition: the mark or feeling left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 印象；印痕。按压留下的东西。

entries.definition: the forced recruitment of sailors.
entries.definitionCN: 强征（旧义）。历史用法。

entries.definition: to state or send quickly. Nearly the same shape, opposite prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 表达；快递。形状几乎相同，前缀相反。

entries.definition: to impress so strongly that one is speechless.
entries.definitionCN: 使震惊。强到说不出话。

entries.definition: to affect strongly, as a thought striking someone.
entries.definitionCN: 打动。如想法击中某人。

entries.definition: to press a mark on paper or metal.
entries.definitionCN: 盖章。在纸或金属上压印。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into im + press, keep the wax-seal image and reuse impressed by.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 im 加 press，保留蜡封意象，并复用 impressed by。

normal.en: im + press: the world presses on you and leaves a mark.
normal.cn: im 加 press：世界压在你身上，留下印记。

normal.en: be impressed by is the standard passive frame.
normal.cn: be impressed by 是标准被动句型。

normal.en: impress on someone means to stamp an idea into memory.
normal.cn: impress on someone 指把想法盖进记忆。

normal.en: impressing the neighbors is the fake version of impressing.
normal.cn: impressing the neighbors 是 impress 的虚假版本。

normal.en: impressment pressed bodies, not wax; a dark historic sense.
normal.cn: impressment 压的是人不是蜡；黑暗的历史义项。

abstract.en: One image: a seal pressed into warm wax.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：印章压进温热的蜡。

abstract.en: To impress is to leave a mark that argues for you.
abstract.cn: impress 是留下一个替你说话的印记。

abstract.en: Marks differ: wax marks, mind marks, forged marks.
abstract.cn: 印记有别：蜡上的、心里的、伪造的。

examples.en: The documentary impressed me deeply.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片令我印象深刻。

examples.en: The jeweler impressed his mark into the gold.
examples.cn: 珠宝匠把标记压进金子里。

examples.en: She tried to impress the panel with her research.
examples.cn: 她试图用研究打动评审团。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一姆普瑞斯」：一按，噗——印记落在你心里， impressed！

root: 拉丁语 in-（入）+ premere「压」→ imprimere「压入」→ impressio「印记」→ 古法语 → 中古英语 impress「盖章→铭刻于心」；现代英语以钦佩义为主。

sensesIntro.en: Impress presses: a seal into wax, an idea into memory, admiration into a mind, and, in history, men into ships.
sensesIntro.cn: impress 就是按压：印章入蜡、观念入心、钦佩入脑，历史上还有强征入伍。

core.en: Hard contact that leaves a lasting copy of itself.
core.cn: 坚硬的接触，留下自身持久的复制品。

branches.en: ADMIRATION: her reply impressed the judges.
branches.cn: 钦佩：她的回答令评委折服。

branches.en: STAMP: the seal impressed on the certificate.
branches.cn: 盖印：印章压上证书。

branches.en: MEMORY: impressing discipline on the team.
branches.cn: 记忆：让纪律深植全队。

branches.en: SHOW: impressing the neighbors on purpose.
branches.cn: 做秀：刻意给邻居留下印象。

branches.en: FORCE: impressment of sailors into the navy.
branches.cn: 强征：将水手强征入海军。

intro.en: Impress keeps the Latin press at its heart; the family adds impression, impressive, impressed and the partner express.
intro.cn: impress 的核心是拉丁语的「压」；词族加上 impression、impressive、impressed 及反前缀的 express。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the pressing verb and the noun for the mark it leaves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示按压动词与其留下的印记名词。

items.meaning: to fill with admiration; to stamp
items.example: The view impressed the travelers.

items.meaning: a mark or a feeling left behind
items.example: First impressions matter.
An impressive list of wins.
items.exampleCN: 一份令人赞叹的胜绩清单。

items.example: The jury was impressed by the design.
items.exampleCN: 评审团对设计印象深刻。

items.example: The pianist kept impressing the crowd.
Impressment caused riots in ports.
She expressed her thanks.

items.meaning: the art style of capturing impressions
items.example: Impressionism changed painting.

definition_en: to make or become better
core_image: 把一块毛坯石一点点磨亮
scene: 训练日记上写满记录。Practicing every morning improved his serve.
sceneCN: 这里 improve 是「改进、提高」（第 1 个义项：使更好）；句意：每天早晨的练习提高了他的发球水平。

senses.title: To make better
senses.definition: to raise the quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 提升某物的品质
senses.example: The new plan improved the workflow.
senses.exampleCN: 新方案改进了工作流程。
senses.why: A rough stone is ground brighter stroke by stroke.
senses.whyCN: 毛坯石被一刀刀磨亮。

senses.title: To become better
senses.definition: to become better in quality or condition
senses.definitionCN: 品质或状态变好
senses.example: Her eyesight improved after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后她的视力好转了。
senses.why: The grinding continues even without a hand behind it.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有手在背后，打磨也在继续。

senses.title: To use an opportunity well
senses.definition: to make good use of a chance or time
senses.definitionCN: 好好利用机会或时间
senses.example: He improved the pause to study the menu.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用间歇研究了菜单。
senses.why: Time is a stone too: grind it into something valuable.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是块石头：把它磨成有价值的东西。

senses.title: To raise in value
senses.definition: to increase the worth of land or property
senses.definitionCN: 增加土地或财产的价值
senses.example: They improved the house before selling.
senses.exampleCN: 卖房前他们先翻修了房子。
senses.why: A better stone sells for more; polish adds price.
senses.whyCN: 更好的石头卖价更高；打磨即增值。

intro.en: Improve grew out of the old phrase emprowe, to turn a profit, from Old French prowe, profit or advantage, related to English boot in the old sense of advantage. The business root still lives in the word: to improve is to add gain.
intro.cn: improve 由旧短语 emprowe「获利润」发展而来，出自古法语 prowe「利润、益处」，与英语 boot 的旧义「益处」相关。商业根源仍活在词中：improve 即增益。

items.en: Old French prowe meant profit or advantage, itself from a word for benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 prowe 意为利润或益处，源自表示利益的词。

items.en: The phrase en prou, to one's profit, prefixed the verb emprower.
items.cn: 短语 en prou「于己有利」前缀出动词 emprower。

items.en: Middle English improven first meant to turn land to profit by enclosure.
items.cn: 中古英语 improven 先指圈地使土地产生收益。

items.en: The profit sense widened to making anything better.
items.cn: 利润义扩大为使一切变得更好。

items.en: The nineteenth century standardized improvement in industry, education and health.
items.cn: 十九世纪 improvement 在工业、教育与卫生领域标准化。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the improve family and the false cousin approve. The meaning group compares bettering words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 improve 词族与假表亲 approve；词义组比较表示变好的词。

entries.definition: the act or result of improving.
entries.definitionCN: 改进；改善。本词的名词。

entries.definition: to accept or agree. Looks close but comes from Latin probare, to test.
entries.definitionCN: 批准。字形相近，但源自拉丁语 probare「检验」。

entries.definition: a person or thing that improves.
entries.definitionCN: 改进者。表人后缀形式。

entries.definition: to add value or strength to something good.
entries.definitionCN: 增强。为已有的好加值。

entries.definition: to make finer and more polished.
entries.definitionCN: 精炼。做得更精细更雅。

entries.definition: to move forward toward a better state.
entries.definitionCN: 进步。朝更好状态前进。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split improve into im + prove, reuse the profit root and warn against approve.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 improve 拆成 im 加 prove，复用利润词根，并警示 approve。

normal.en: Old root said profit: to improve is to add gain, not just change.
normal.cn: 旧词根说利润：improve 是增益，不只是改变。

normal.en: improve on takes a base: improve on last year's record.
normal.cn: improve on 带基数：超越去年的纪录。

normal.en: Do not swap improve and approve; one makes better, one says yes.
normal.cn: 不要互换 improve 与 approve：一个变好，一个点头。

normal.en: improvement is the noun box that stores the change.
normal.cn: improvement 是收纳变化的名词盒子。

normal.en: improved marks the finished grind: an improved engine.
normal.cn: improved 标记打磨完成：improved engine。

abstract.en: One image: a dull stone growing a bright edge.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：钝石长出锋刃。

abstract.en: Improvement is profit paid in quality.
abstract.cn: improvement 是以品质支付的利润。

abstract.en: Two directions: you improve things, or things improve themselves.
abstract.cn: 两个方向：你改进事物，或事物自行好转。

examples.en: The software improved greatly after the update.
examples.cn: 更新后软件大有改善。

examples.en: Reading daily will improve your vocabulary.
examples.cn: 每天阅读会提高你的词汇量。

examples.en: The city improved the park with new paths and lights.
examples.cn: 市政府用新步道和路灯升级了公园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一姆普如夫」：一母（一条母线）普普通通，如（入）夫（工厂）打磨就 improve。

root: 古法语 prowe「利润、益处」→ 短语 en prou → emprower「使获利」→ 中古英语 improven「圈地获利」→ 现代英语 improve「改进、好转」；与 approve（拉丁 probare）无同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Improve grinds better: objects, bodies, chances and property all take a brighter edge.
sensesIntro.cn: improve 打磨一切更好：物件、身体、机会与财产都被磨出更亮的光。

core.en: A rough thing gaining value under steady grinding.
core.cn: 毛坯在持续打磨下增值。

branches.en: MAKING: the new plan improved the workflow.
branches.cn: 使动：新方案改进了流程。

branches.en: BECOMING: eyesight improved after the operation.
branches.cn: 自动：术后视力好转。

branches.en: OPPORTUNITY: improving a pause to study.
branches.cn: 机会：利用间隙学习。

branches.en: VALUE: improving a house before selling.
branches.cn: 增值：卖前翻修房屋。

branches.en: TREND: improving steadily, year over year.
branches.cn: 趋势：逐年稳步提升。

intro.en: Improve adds a small family: improvement, improved, improver, with approve as the misleading neighbor.
intro.cn: improve 的词族不大：improvement、improved、improver，旁边还有易误导的 approve。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries section stays empty: the family is French and Anglo-French in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空：词族出自法语与盎格鲁-法语。

items.example: The route improved with new signs.
items.exampleCN: 新路牌改善了路线体验。

items.meaning: the act or result of improving
items.example: The improvement showed in the numbers.
An improved model shipped in May.
The patient is improving daily.

items.meaning: one who or that which improves
items.example: Steam was a great improver of travel.
items.exampleCN: 蒸汽机大大改进了出行。

items.example: The system is improvable at low cost.
The board approved the budget.
Self-improvement books line the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 书架上排满自我提升类书。

definition_zh: 在……里；进入；在……期间；流行的；时髦的
definition_en: inside or within a place or time, into it, or fashionable
core_image: 一个圈：圈内为在，跨过线为入
scene: 教室门口的磁力线。The teacher asked everyone to be in the classroom before the bell.
sceneCN: 这里 in 是「在……里面」（第 1 个义项：处于某范围之内）；句意：老师要求大家在铃响前到教室里坐好。

derivatives.zh: 入站的；进来的；复合构词

senses.title: Inside a space
senses.definition: within a place or area
senses.definitionCN: 在某地点或范围之内
senses.example: The keys are in the drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙在抽屉里。
senses.why: Draw a circle: what the circle holds is in.
senses.whyCN: 画一个圈：圈住的东西就是 in。

senses.title: Into a space
senses.definition: moving from outside to inside
senses.definitionCN: 从外向内移动
senses.example: She walked in without knocking.
senses.exampleCN: 她没敲门就走了进来。
senses.why: The circle gains a member: the line is crossed.
senses.whyCN: 圈子吸纳新成员：线被跨过。

senses.title: During a period or after a time
senses.definition: within a length of time, or after it passes
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内，或一段时间之后
senses.example: The bus arrives in five minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车五分钟后到。
senses.why: Time is a circle too: the event falls inside its rim.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是圆圈：事件落进它的边缘内。

senses.title: A state or condition
senses.definition: in a state such as love, trouble or silence
senses.definitionCN: 处于恋爱、麻烦或沉默等状态
senses.example: The village lay in peace that night.
senses.exampleCN: 那晚村庄安宁无事。
senses.why: The circle drawn around a feeling holds the person.
senses.whyCN: 围着感受画一个圈，把人圈在其中。

senses.title: Fashionable or at home
senses.definition: in fashion, or present at a place
senses.definitionCN: 时兴的，或人在某处
senses.example: Purple is in this season.
senses.exampleCN: 紫色这季正流行。
senses.why: The circle of style accepts a color, a word, or the owner back home.
senses.whyCN: 潮流的圈接纳一种颜色、一个词，或把主人圈回家中。

intro.en: In is one of the oldest English words, from Old English in, on, within, from a Germanic root shared with Latin in and Greek en. The circle of inside and the movement into have lived together since the beginning.
intro.cn: in 是最古老的英语词之一，来自古英语 in「在、于内」，与拉丁语 in、希腊语 en 同出日耳曼词根。「在内之圈」与「进入之动」从一开始就并存。

items.en: The Germanic root ina gave Old Frisian and Old Saxon in, matching Latin in and Greek en.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 ina 给出古弗里西亚语与古撒克逊语 in，对应拉丁语 in 与希腊语 en。

items.en: Old English in served as preposition and adverb for both rest and motion.
items.cn: 古英语 in 兼作介词与副词，兼顾静止与移动。

items.en: Middle English in compounded freely: income, indeed, inland.
items.cn: 中古英语 in 大量构词：income、indeed、inland。

items.en: Early modern English fixed the time sense in five minutes and the state sense in love.
items.cn: 近代英语固定了时间义 in five minutes 与状态义 in love。

items.en: The fashion sense is in emerged in the twentieth century, and computing added input and log in.
items.cn: 流行义 is in 出现于二十世纪，计算机领域又加了 input 与 log in。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the short direction words. The meaning group compares inside words and the fashion sense.
note.cn: 形近组收录短小的方位词；词义组比较「在内」类词与流行义。

entries.definition: a small hotel. Sounds the same but comes from a word for dwelling.
entries.definitionCN: 小旅馆。同音异源，出自「居所」一词。

entries.definition: resting on a surface; the partner preposition of in.
entries.definitionCN: 在……上。in 的搭档介词。

entries.definition: the full motion form of in.
entries.definitionCN: into。in 的完整移动形式。

entries.definition: in the inner part; more concrete than in.
entries.definitionCN: 在内。比 in 更具体。

entries.definition: inside the limits of, often with time or rules.
entries.definitionCN: 在……之内。常与时间或规则连用。

entries.definition: fashionable right now; matches the adjective sense.
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的。对应流行义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks draw the circle image, pair in and out, and reuse the idiom in and in fashion.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩画出圆圈意象，配对 in 与 out，并复用惯用语与流行义。

normal.en: in is a circle; out is everything it leaves outside.
normal.cn: in 是一个圈；out 是圈外的一切。

normal.en: in five minutes counts time falling into the rim.
normal.cn: in five minutes 是把时间计进圈边。

normal.en: in love draws the circle around a feeling.
normal.cn: in love 用圈圈住一种感受。

normal.en: be in means at home or in fashion, depending on the talk.
normal.cn: be in 视语境指在家或正流行。

normal.en: into is in plus motion: she walked into the room.
normal.cn: into 是 in 加移动：她走进房间。

abstract.en: One image: a hoop; anything inside it is in.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一个圈；圈内的都是 in。

abstract.en: In is the smallest map you will ever draw.
abstract.cn: in 是你能画出的最小的地图。

abstract.en: Fashion is a circle too: things go in and out of it.
abstract.cn: 潮流也是圈：事物进出其中。

examples.en: The report is in the top drawer.
examples.cn: 报告在顶层抽屉里。

examples.en: We moved in last spring.
examples.cn: 我们去年春天搬了进来。

examples.en: Loose denim is in among teenagers this year.
examples.cn: 宽松牛仔裤今年在青少年中很流行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「硬」：硬把自己塞进去，就在里面了——in。

root: 古英语 in「在、于内」，日耳曼词根，与拉丁语 in、希腊语 en 同源；兼表静止（在内）与移动（进入），后发展出状态、时间与流行诸义。

sensesIntro.en: In draws circles: around space, motion, time, feelings and fashion.
sensesIntro.cn: in 画圈：围住空间、运动、时间、感受与潮流。

core.en: A circle drawn around what is held, joined or kept.
core.cn: 围住所容纳、所接纳、所保存之物的圆圈。

branches.en: SPACE: the keys are in the drawer.
branches.cn: 空间：钥匙在抽屉里。

branches.en: MOTION: she walked in.
branches.cn: 运动：她走了进来。

branches.en: TIME: arriving in five minutes.
branches.cn: 时间：五分钟后到达。

branches.en: STATE: in love, in trouble, in peace.
branches.cn: 状态：in love、in trouble、in peace。

branches.en: STYLE: purple is in this season.
branches.cn: 潮流：紫色这季正流行。

intro.en: In compounds endlessly: input, inbound, income, inland; as a prefix it can also mean not, as in invisible.
intro.cn: in 可大量构词：input、inbound、income、inland；作前缀时还可表否定，如 invisible。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the same circle: Latin in kept the identical meaning inside its language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示同一个圈：拉丁语 in 在其语言中含义相同。

items.example: The letter is in the bag.

items.meaning: what is put in; data entered
items.example: Check the input before running.
The inbound flight landed early.
Their income doubled.
Inland towns grew fast.
The ink was invisible.

items.meaning: a turn in cricket; one's span of action
items.example: His innings ended at noon.
items.exampleCN: 他的发言时段在正午结束。

items.example: She knows the ins and outs of the case.
items.exampleCN: 她了解此案的来龙去脉。

definition_en: a unit of length equal to 2.54 centimeters, or to move very slowly
core_image: 尺子上最小的一格，一寸一寸挪
scene: 木工房里拉卷尺。The carpenter measured the shelf to the last inch.
sceneCN: 这里 inch 是「英寸」（第 1 个义项：长度单位）；句意：木匠把书架量到了最后一英寸。

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.definition: a unit of length, 2.54 centimeters
senses.definitionCN: 长度单位，2.54 厘米
senses.example: The screen measures twenty inches across.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕对角线长二十英寸。
senses.why: The thumb joint of the old ruler: the smallest named step.
senses.whyCN: 旧尺上的拇指关节：最小的命名刻度。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a very small distance or degree
senses.definitionCN: 极小的距离或程度
senses.example: The bullet missed him by an inch.
senses.exampleCN: 子弹差一寸就打中他。
senses.why: One smallest step decides a whole outcome.
senses.whyCN: 最小的一步决定整个结局。

senses.title: To move very slowly
senses.definition: to move slowly and by small degrees
senses.definitionCN: 以极小的步幅缓慢移动
senses.example: The truck inched through the narrow gate.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车缓缓挤过窄门。
senses.why: The unit becomes a verb: advance one smallest step at a time.
senses.whyCN: 单位转动词：一次只挪最小的一步。

senses.title: Rainfall or snowfall measure
senses.definition: a unit for measuring rain or snow depth
senses.definitionCN: 测量降雨或积雪深度的单位
senses.example: Three inches of snow fell overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜下了三英寸厚的雪。
senses.why: The ruler is lifted from wood to weather.
senses.whyCN: 尺子从木工活被举到天气里。

senses.title: Every inch: completely
senses.definition: in every respect; completely
senses.definitionCN: 在每个方面；完全地
senses.example: She looked every inch a captain.
senses.exampleCN: 她看上去完全是个船长。
senses.why: Every smallest step of the ruler adds up to the whole picture.
senses.whyCN: 尺上每一小格加起来就是全貌。

intro.en: Inch comes from Old English ynce, borrowed from Latin uncia, a twelfth, the twelfth part of a Roman foot. The same Latin word gave English ounce; inch and ounce are twins.
intro.cn: inch 来自古英语 ynce，借自拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」，即罗马尺的十二分之一。同一个词也给了英语 ounce；inch 与 ounce 是孪生词。

items.en: Latin uncia meant a twelfth part, of a foot or of a pound.
items.cn: 拉丁语 uncia 指十二分之一，或指尺或磅。

items.en: The twelfth of a pound became the ounce; the twelfth of a foot became the inch.
items.cn: 一磅的十二分之一成了盎司；一尺的十二分之一成了英寸。

items.en: Old English ynce fixed the borrowing; the inch then matched three barleycorns laid end to end.
items.cn: 古英语 ynce 定型借词；当时的英寸相当于三粒大麦首尾相接。

items.en: Middle English inch settled the spelling and grew the small-amount sense.
items.cn: 中古英语定型拼写，发展出少量义。

items.en: In nineteen fifty-nine the inch was fixed internationally at exactly 2.54 centimeters.
items.cn: 一九五九年英寸在国际上被定为精确的 2.54 厘米。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the inch family and its twin ounce. The meaning group compares small units and small movements.
note.cn: 形近组收录 inch 词族及其孪生词 ounce；词义组比较小单位与小移动。

entries.definition: a unit of weight, from the same Latin uncia.
entries.definitionCN: 盎司。出自同一个拉丁词 uncia。

entries.definition: plural of inch.
entries.definitionCN: 英寸的复数。

entries.definition: a feeling that makes you scratch. One letter apart.
entries.definitionCN: 痒。只差一个字母。

entries.definition: the metric small step; one inch is 2.54 of them.
entries.definitionCN: 厘米。公制的小格；1 英寸等于 2.54 厘米。

entries.definition: to move slowly and quietly, close to the verb sense.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢潜行。接近动词义项。

entries.definition: a tiny amount or part.
entries.definitionCN: 一小部分。指极小的量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link inch and ounce, use inch by inch and flag the itch trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把 inch 与 ounce 相连，用 inch by inch，并标记 itch 陷阱。

normal.en: inch and ounce are twins: both from Latin uncia, a twelfth.
normal.cn: inch 与 ounce 是孪生词：都来自拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」。

normal.en: inch by inch is the classic patience phrase.
normal.cn: inch by inch 是经典的耐心短语。

normal.en: The verb inched shows tiny progress: the truck inched forward.
normal.cn: 动词 inched 表现微小进展：卡车缓缓前行。

normal.en: Every inch a leader means completely a leader.
normal.cn: every inch a leader 意为彻头彻尾的领袖。

normal.en: Do not mix inch and itch: one measures, one scratches.
normal.cn: 别混淆 inch 与 itch：一个测量，一个挠痒。

abstract.en: One image: a thumb pressing the smallest mark on a ruler.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：拇指按在尺上最小的一格。

abstract.en: An inch is the step between fail and triumph.
abstract.cn: 一英寸就是失败与胜利之间的一步。

abstract.en: Slow verbs love this word: inch, creep, edge.
abstract.cn: 慢动词偏爱这个词：inch、creep、edge。

examples.en: He is about six feet two inches tall.
examples.cn: 他身高约六英尺二英寸。

examples.en: The turtle inched across the road.
examples.cn: 乌龟缓缓爬过马路。

examples.en: They won by inches in the final seconds.
examples.cn: 最后几秒他们以毫厘之差获胜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「因尺」：因为尺子上一小格就是一英寸， inch。

root: 拉丁语 uncia「十二分之一」（罗马尺的 1/12）→ 古英语 ynce「英寸」→ 中古英语 inch；与 ounce 同源孪生；动词义「缓慢移动」与少量义为英语内部发展。

sensesIntro.en: Inch is the smallest ruler step: a length, a near-miss, a slow crawl, a rainfall measure, and the whole when every step is counted.
sensesIntro.cn: inch 是尺上最小的格：一段长度、一次险胜、一次缓行、一份降水量，以及每格都数时的全部。

core.en: The smallest named step on the ruler of distance, effort and outcome.
core.cn: 距离、努力与结局之尺上最小的命名刻度。

branches.en: LENGTH: twenty inches across.
branches.cn: 长度：二十英寸宽。

branches.en: MARGIN: missed by an inch.
branches.cn: 毫厘：差一寸没打中。

branches.en: MOTION: the truck inched through.
branches.cn: 移动：卡车缓缓挤过。

branches.en: WEATHER: three inches of snow.
branches.cn: 降水：三英寸的雪。

branches.en: COMPLETENESS: every inch a captain.
branches.cn: 完全：every inch a captain。

intro.en: Inch builds inches, inching and compounds like inchworm and half-inch.
intro.cn: inch 构成 inches、inching 及 inchworm、half-inch 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the twelfth-part noun that split into inch and ounce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示那个分裂为英寸与盎司的「十二分之一」名词。

items.meaning: a unit of length; a tiny amount
items.example: The gap narrowed to an inch.
Six inches of rope were left.
The queue was inching forward.
The car inched out of the lot.

items.meaning: a caterpillar that moves in inch-steps
items.example: An inchworm crossed the leaf.

items.meaning: half an inch; slang for steal
items.example: A half-inch bolt held the plate.
items.exampleCN: 半英寸螺栓固定着钢板。

items.example: His pass was inch-perfect.
An ounce of prevention helps.
items.exampleCN: 一分预防胜过一分救治。

latinEntries.meaning: a twelfth part; one-twelfth of a foot or pound
latinEntries.meaningCN: 十二分之一；罗马尺或磅的十二分之一
